rows.Notes: Known as "The Southland Strangler" and "The Westside Rapist"

rows.Name: Thomas, Regis Deon
rows.Notes: Gang member who killed three people, including two police officers, in Compton, Los Angeles

rows.Name: Thompson, William Paul
rows.Notes: Robbed and killed two men at a bar, then killed another man while on the run

rows.Name: Thornburg, Jason Alan
rows.Notes: Murdered and dismembered three people in Texas in September 2021; additionally confessed to killing his girlfriend and his roommate

rows.Name: Toole, Ottis
rows.Notes: Accomplice of Henry Lee Lucas ; claimed to have murdered Adam Walsh

rows.Name: Toppan, Jane
rows.Notes: Known as "Jolly Jane"; nurse who poisoned both patients and family members in Massachusetts

rows.Name: Torrence, Michael
rows.Notes: Robbed and killed two men with his brother and his wife; later killed a prostitute in Charleston during an argument

rows.Name: Travis, Maury
rows.Notes: Suspected of kidnapping, torturing and killing women at his home in Ferguson, Missouri

rows.Name: Trawick, Jack
rows.Notes: Executed for murdering a student in 1992. Confessed to killing five to 14 women in Alabama and other states, but only three victims were confirmed.

rows.Name: Ture Jr., Joseph
rows.Notes: Murdered a family of four and two other women in Minnesota

rows.Name: Turner, Chester
rows.Notes: Convicted of murdering ten women and a viable unborn baby in South Los Angeles

rows.Name: Turner, Douglas
rows.Notes: Convicted of killing a family of three, then killed six inmates in prison

rows.Name: Urdiales, Andrew
rows.Notes: United States Marine who murdered women in Indiana, Illinois and California

rows.Name: Vann, Darren Deon
rows.Notes: Indiana murderer who killed seven women; five of which were found in abandoned structures in the city of Gary

rows.Name: Vaultz, Horace Van
rows.Notes: Raped and murdered women across California; his home contained photographs of over twenty potential victims

rows.Name: Van Dyke, David
rows.Notes: Murdered six people in their homes in Milwaukee, Wisconsin

rows.Name: Vermilya, Louise
rows.Notes: Charges dismissed

rows.Name: Victor, Clarence
rows.Notes: Killed three people in Omaha, Nebraska , the latter two while on parole

rows.Name: Villarreal, David
rows.Notes: Gay drifter who tortured and murdered acquaintances in San Antonio and Dallas

rows.Name: Wade, Joshua
rows.Notes: Murdered people across Alaska during angry outbursts or robberies

rows.Name: Wagner, Kenny
rows.Notes: Murdered three police officers and two other men during prison escapes and as a fugitive

rows.Name: Waldrop, Billy
rows.Notes: Killed an elderly man during a robbery after serving time in prison for two other murders

rows.Name: Walker, Anthony Guy
rows.Notes: Career criminal who murdered mainly across Lenawee County, Michigan

rows.Name: Walker, Gary Alan
rows.Notes: Known as the "Roaming Rapist"; murdered four women and one man in Oklahoma and Kentucky

rows.Name: Walker, Tracy
rows.Notes: Killed a security guard during an argument; released and later killed fellow homeless people in Rancho Dominguez

rows.Name: Wallace, Henry Louis
rows.Notes: Known as "The Taco Bell Strangler"; preyed on women in and around Charlotte, North Carolina

rows.Name: Walton, Edward
rows.Notes: Confessed to murdering five people across five states

rows.Name: Walls, Frank Athen
rows.Notes: Confessed to murdering five people across Ocean City , Florida

rows.Name: Ward, Ronald James
rows.Notes: Murdered at least three women and one man in three states, in the span of four months

rows.Name: Wardrip, Faryion
rows.Notes: Serial rapist who assaulted and murdered women in Wichita Falls , Texas and the surrounding counties. Death sentence currently under appeal

rows.Name: Warren, Edward Delon
rows.Notes: Murdered a couple in Brookings, Oregon ; later linked via DNA to an unsolved murder in Portland

rows.Name: Warren, Lesley Eugene
rows.Notes: Known as "The Babyface Killer"; raped and murdered women in New York and the Carolinas

rows.Name: Washington, Steven
rows.Notes: Known as "The Window-Screen Rapist"; juvenile who raped and killed elderly women around St. Petersburg, Florida

rows.Name: Watson, Alexander Wayne
rows.Notes: Raped, stabbed and strangled women in two Maryland counties

rows.Name: Watts, Carl Eugene
rows.Notes: Known as "The Sunday Morning Slasher"; assaulted, tortured and murdered teenaged girls and young women in Michigan and Texas

rows.Name: Webb, Emanuel Lovell
rows.Notes: Known as "The East End Killer"; raped and killed four women in Connecticut and a fifth woman in Georgia

rows.Name: Weldon, Stewart
rows.Notes: Tortured and murdered women in Springfield, Massachusetts

rows.Name: Wells, William
rows.Notes: Murdered his wife and four other people in 2003. Also killed two prisoners, one in 2011 and another in 2019 respectively.

rows.Name: Werner, Karl F.
rows.Notes: Murdered teenage girls in Santa Clara County, California

rows.Name: Wheeler-Weaver, Khalil
rows.Notes: Killed women he met through dating apps in Orange, New Jersey

rows.Name: Whisenhant, Thomas
rows.Notes: Kidnapped and murdered female clerks from convenience stores in Mobile County, Alabama

rows.Name: White, Larry Lamont
rows.Notes: Shot and killed women in Louisville, Kentucky , during apparent robberies

rows.Name: White, Nathaniel
rows.Notes: Confessed to bludgeoning and stabbing six women to death in Hudson Valley, New York , while on parole

rows.Name: White, Robert
rows.Notes: Sexually assaulted and beat three women to death in Hartford, Connecticut , while on parole for an earlier murder

rows.Name: Whiteling, Sarah
rows.Notes: Known as "The Wholesale Poisoner"

rows.Name: Whitten, Hattie
rows.Notes: Maine woman who poisoned her husband and two children

rows.Name: Wickline, William
rows.Notes: Known as "The Butcher"; drug addict who killed people in West Virginia and Ohio, dismembering and beheading their bodies post-mortem

rows.Name: Wilder, Christopher
rows.Notes: Known as "The Beauty Queen Killer"; Australian man who abducted and murdered women across the US

rows.Name: Wiley, Nicholas
rows.Notes: Known as "The Syracuse Serial Killer"; sex offender who confessed to killing seven people in Syracuse, New York

rows.Name: Williams, Dorothy
rows.Notes: Robbed and killed elderly people to support her heroin addiction

rows.Name: Williams, Kenneth Dewayne
rows.Notes: Killed two people on the same day, then killed two more people after escaping from prison

rows.Name: Williams, Laron
rows.Fate: Murdered in prison by fellow death row inmates
rows.Notes: Strangled a prostitute in Nashville, Tennessee ; later escaped from prison, murdering a police officer and priest; suspect in other murders across several states

rows.Name: Williams, Leslie Allen
rows.Notes: Necrophile who killed and raped at least four women in Michigan while on parole for rape from 1991 to 1992.

rows.Name: Williams, Ronald Turney
rows.Notes: Criminal who murdered a police officer in 1975, another police officer while escaping from prison, and a final victim while he was a fugitive

rows.Name: Williams, Scott
rows.Notes: Killed women in Charlotte and Monroe, North Carolina

rows.Name: Williamson, Thomas Andrew
rows.Notes: Murdered four people in Illinois and Missouri, including his wife

rows.Name: Willie, Robert Lee
rows.Notes: Murdered at least three people in Louisiana

rows.Name: Wimberly, Anthony
rows.Notes: Murdered three women in Oakland during a crime spree

rows.Name: Wise, Martha
rows.Notes: Poisoned seventeen members of her own family in Ohio

rows.Name: Wood, Cathy
rows.Notes: Accomplice of Gwendolyn Graham ; nurse's aide that preyed on elderly women in a Walker, Michigan nursing home

rows.Name: Wood, David Leonard
rows.Notes: Known as "The Desert Killer"; raped and murdered young girls and women in El Paso, Texas , burying their bodies in the desert afterwards

rows.Name: Wood, Frederick Charles
rows.Notes: Violent habitual criminal who killed people in various New York cities, starting at age 14

rows.Name: Woodfield, Randall
rows.Notes: Known as "The I-5 Killer" and "The I-5 Bandit"; serial rapist, kidnapper, robber and burglar who preyed on women along the Interstate 5 corridor running through Washington, Oregon and California

rows.Name: Woodward, Arthur T.
rows.Notes: Perpetrator of the Osage Indian murders

rows.Name: Wooten, Charles
rows.Notes: Killed two gas station attendants in Fort Worth during robberies; paroled, and later killed his father during an argument

rows.Name: Wright, Douglas Franklin
rows.Notes: First criminal executed by lethal injection in Oregon

rows.Name: Wuornos, Aileen
rows.Notes: Known as the "Damsel of Death"; shot seven men to death in Florida between 1989 and 1990

rows.Name: Yates, Robert Lee
rows.Fate: Sentenced to death; commuted to life imprisonment
rows.Notes: Known as "The Grocery Bag Killer"; targeted women in and around Spokane, Washington

rows.Name: Zarinsky, Robert
rows.Notes: Murdered three teenage girls in Monmouth County, New Jersey ; was also acquitted in the murder of a police officer

table_name.header_chain: List of serial killers in the United States > Unidentified serial killers
table_name.additional_text: This is a list of unidentified serial killers who committed crimes within the United States.

rows.Name: Alphabet murders
rows.Notes: Also known as the "Double Initial Murders"; murders of three young girls in the Rochester, New York area in the early 1970s

rows.Name: Ann Arbor Hospital murders
rows.Notes: Poisonings of ten patients at the Veteran's Administration Hospital in 1975. Two nurses, Filipina Narciso and Leonora Perez, were convicted but a new trial was ordered because of prosecutorial misconduct. The prosecution chose to drop the charges rather than retry.

rows.Name: Atlanta child murders
rows.Notes: A series of murders committed in Atlanta, Georgia, between July 1979 and May 1981. Over the two-year period, at least twenty-eight children, adolescents, and adults were killed. Wayne Williams was charged and sentenced for the two adult murders, with twenty-four of the other murders attributed to him.

rows.Name: Atlanta Lover's Lane Murders
rows.Notes: A series of unsolved shootings of couples in Atlanta from January to March 1977

rows.Name: Atlanta Ripper
rows.Notes: Mystery murderer(s) of fifteen Atlanta women in 1911

rows.Name: Axeman of New Orleans
rows.Notes: Responsible for the deaths of six or seven people in New Orleans and the surrounding areas from 1918 to 1919

rows.Name: Bag murders
rows.Notes: Murders and dismemberment of gay men in Lower Manhattan , whose body parts were wrapped in garbage bags and thrown into the Hudson River ; convicted murderer Paul Bateson was a prime suspect in the killings, but never charged

rows.Name: Bigfoot Killer
rows.Notes: Raped and murdered sex workers in Detroit; nicknamed derived from the suspect's large hands and feet

rows.Name: Boca Raton murders
rows.Notes: Three unsolved murders of women committed at the Town Center Mall in Boca Raton, Florida in 2007

rows.Name: Boston Strangler
rows.Notes: 1960s deaths of thirteen women (five young, eight older), mostly with their own stockings as ligature. Albert DeSalvo confessed to the murders, but was never indicted; DNA evidence tested in 2013 suggested his guilt in one of the cases

rows.Name: Bouncing Ball Killer
rows.Notes: Series of murders targeted towards elderly women in Los Angeles; convicted murderer Raymond Ward Clemmons confessed to the murders, but he was never charged due to a lie detector proving he was being untruthful

rows.Name: Bra murders
rows.Notes: Strangulations of five sex workers in Stamford, Connecticut ; schizophrenic preacher Benjamin Franklin Miller was prosecuted for the crimes, but acquitted by reason of insanity, leaving his true guilt in question

rows.Name: Castration serial murders
rows.Notes: Series of murders of men who were shot in the back of the head and then castrated post-mortem

rows.Name: Charlie Chop-off
rows.Notes: Murders of five boys in Manhattan in 1972 and 1973. A mental patient confessed to one slashing death. Four stabbings also involving mutilation remain unsolved

rows.Name: Chicago Strangler
rows.Notes: Raped and strangled predominantly African-American prostitutes and other vulnerable women in Chicago; could possibly be multiple serial killers

rows.Name: Cincinnati Strangler
rows.Notes: Raped and strangled seven mostly elderly women in Cincinnati , Ohio , between 1965 and 1966; Cab driver Posteal Laskey Jr. is commonly believed to be culprit

rows.Name: Cleveland Torso Murderer
rows.Notes: Also known as the "Mad Butcher of Kingsbury Run"; responsible for 12–13 murders in the Cleveland , Ohio area in the 1930s

rows.Name: Colonial Parkway Killer
rows.Notes: Believed to have murdered at least eight people in Virginia between 1986 and 1989; left three couples dead and one couple missing and presumed dead. In January 2024, authorities announced that at least two of the murders had been conclusively linked to an official suspect, Alan W. Wilmer Sr., a local fisherman who died in 2017. Wilmer was also identified as a suspect in an unrelated third murder.

rows.Name: Columbus murders
rows.Notes: Three fatal shootings committed in Columbus and West Jefferson

rows.Name: Connecticut River Valley Killer
rows.Notes: Stabbed at least six women to death in New England in the 1980s, severely injured one

rows.Name: Cumminsville Killer
rows.Notes: Murdered and mutilated women in the Cincinnati neighborhood of South Cumminsville

rows.Name: Dayton Strangler
rows.Notes: Murdered five women and one man in Dayton, Ohio , in the early 20th century; one man was wrongfully convicted for the murders

rows.Name: Denver Prostitute Killer
rows.Notes: Abducted, raped and strangled young girls and women around Denver and its various suburbs

rows.Name: Denver Strangler
rows.Notes: Strangled three prostitutes in Denver in ten weeks; also thought to be responsible in two more murders

rows.Name: Doodler
rows.Notes: Sketched then stabbed to death gay men in San Francisco, California in the 1970s

rows.Name: Dr. No
rows.Notes: Suspected of raping and strangling prostitutes alongside the Interstate 71 ; his first suspected victim is Marcia King , who was identified in 2018. Samuel Legg III, a trucker, has been arrested and charged but thus far (as of 2020) is incompetent to stand trial. He is receiving psychiatric treatment while they try to restore competency.

rows.Name: Eastbound Strangler
rows.Notes: Murdered four women near Atlantic City, New Jersey , in 2006.

rows.Name: Edgecombe County serial killer
rows.Notes: Murders of nine women and disappearance of another since 2005 around Rocky Mount, North Carolina. Antwan Pittman has been convicted in one case

rows.Name: Essex County prostitute killings
rows.Notes: Murders of at least fourteen women involved with prostitution in Essex County, New Jersey . Multiple perpetrators are suspected, and in 1998 Harrison Hogue was arrested for one of the murders but was ruled incompetent to stand trial.

rows.Name: Flat-Tire murders
rows.Notes: Killed young girls and women in Broward and Miami-Dade Counties by offering help with fixing their car tires, before he sexually assaulted them and drowned them in canals

rows.Name: Flint Serial Slasher
rows.Notes: Stabbing attacks against mostly small-framed African-American men, with the main area being Flint, Michigan ; an Israeli national, Elias Abuelazam, has been convicted in one of the murders and remains the prime suspect in the other four

rows.Name: Fort Myers Eight murders
rows.Notes: The remains of eight adult men discovered murdered in a wooded area in Fort Myers, Florida , on March 23, 2007. The men are believed to have been at the location since the mid-1990s. Convicted murderer and serial rapist Daniel Conahan has been named as the prime suspect

rows.Name: Frankford Slasher
rows.Notes: Allegedly responsible for nine murders in the Frankford neighborhood of Philadelphia, Pennsylvania; Leonard Christopher was convicted of one murder; another murder was committed in same style while he was incarcerated; believed to still be at large

rows.Name: Freeway Phantom
rows.Notes: Raped and strangled six young women and girls in Washington, D.C., in the early 1970s, dumping their bodies by freeways

rows.Name: Gilgo Beach serial killings
rows.Notes: Suspected of killing eight women, a man and a child since 1996 and dumping their bodies along remote beaches in Suffolk and Nassau County, New York. The killer has been referred to as the Gilgo Beach killer because of the location where the first bodies were found. In July 2023, Rex Heuerman was arrested and has been charged with four of the murders.

rows.Name: Gold Sock Killer
rows.Notes: Strangled a woman and two teenage girls to death with socks in Broward County, Florida between July and August.

rows.Name: Golden Years Murders
rows.Notes: Murders of elderly women in Richmond, Virginia ; murderer Leslie Burchart was convicted for some of the killings, but his guilt is disputed

rows.Name: Great Basin Killer
rows.Notes: Allegedly responsible for the "Great Basin Murders", in which young girls and women were raped and killed across the Great Basin area; initially consisting of nine supposed murders, those have since been solved and attributed to different perpetrators

rows.Name: Gulf Killer
rows.Notes: A series of unsolved murders that occurred primarily in Pasco County, Florida in the 1970s; likely multiple killers

rows.Name: Gypsy Hill killings
rows.Notes: Known as the "San Mateo slasher"; five unsolved killings, of young women in San Mateo County, California , during early 1976; in 2014, the FBI named Rodney Halbower as a person of interest in the Gypsy Hill killings; as of 2018  , he has been convicted in two of the murders

rows.Name: Hog Trail Murders
rows.Notes: Mutilated bodies of young men found in Charlotte County, Florida ; thought to be linked to Daniel Conahan , who was charged and convicted of one of the murders

rows.Name: Harbor City serial shootings
rows.Notes: Shot four black men from his Jeep, three of them fatally

rows.Name: Honolulu Strangler
rows.Notes: Raped and strangled five young women in Hawaii in 1985 and 1986

rows.Name: I-45 Killer
rows.Notes: Strangled four known victims in 1980 and sexually assaulted some. Two of the four women have never been identified.

rows.Name: I-70 killer
rows.Notes: Killed and robbed six store clerks around the Midwestern United States

rows.Name: I-70 Strangler
rows.Notes: Killed gay men and dumped their bodies near I-70; suspected serial killer Herb Baumeister is considered the prime suspect in the case

rows.Name: Jeff Davis 8
rows.Notes: The bodies of eight women were found in swamps and canals surrounding Jennings, Louisiana . Originally thought to be a serial killer, but multiple suspects may be involved

rows.Name: Little Rock serial stabbings
rows.Notes: Random stabbing murders against strangers that occurred in Little Rock, Arkansas

rows.Name: Lone Woman Murders
rows.Notes: Over nine unsolved femicides committed in Los Angeles that involved sexual mutilation, including the famous Black Dahlia murder

rows.Name: Main South Woodsman
rows.Notes: Murdered prostitutes picked up from Worcester 's Main South neighborhood, dumping the bodies in various towns across the state and neighboring Maine . Convicted murderer Alex Scesny is considered the prime suspect, but has never been charged.

rows.Name: The Man from the Train
rows.Notes: Probably Paul Mueller. Killed whole families in their sleep, from the East Coast to the West, arriving and departing by train. Existence (probable but identity unproven) was discovered over 100 years after the murders by analysis of contemporary records, showing a markedly common modus operandi for many previously unconnected crimes.

rows.Name: Miami Strangler
rows.Notes: Murdered at least nine women in Miami , Florida , between 1964 and 1970

rows.Name: Michigan Murders
rows.Notes: Raped, stabbed, and strangled young women between the ages of 13 and 21 in the Washtenaw County area of Michigan. John Norman Collins was convicted of the last murder in the series and strongly suspected to be responsible for all seven murders attributed to the same perpetrator.

rows.Name: Missouri River Killer
rows.Notes: Abducted and killed women and young girls in Kansas City, Missouri , and surrounding areas. The killer was noted for amputating his victims' legs before dumping their remains in the Missouri River . Gregory Breeden, a then-Kansas City resident, remains the prime suspect in the case due to his relations with several of the victims, but he vehemently denied being the killer.

rows.Name: Mulatto Axe Murders
rows.Notes: Axe murders of a minimum of twelve African-American and interracial families along the Southern Pacific railroad line running through Louisiana and Texas. Raymond Barnabet was tried and convicted of the murders of one family. His teenage daughter, Clementine Barnabet was arrested shortly afterwards following the murder of another family and confessed to the murders of thirty-five others. She was later convicted of one murder, but released from prison in 1923. Both convictions have been disputed by historians. No one has ever been charged with the other slayings

rows.Name: Nassau County serial murders
rows.Notes: Murders of five prostitutes committed in the Nassau County area; Allen Gormely, convicted of murdering two prostitutes in Long Beach in 1990, is considered the current prime suspect

rows.Name: New Bedford Highway Killer
rows.Notes: Murders of nine women and disappearance of two others between 1988 and 1989

rows.Name: Oakland County Child Killer
rows.Notes: Also known as the "Babysitter"; responsible for the murders of four or more children in Oakland County, Michigan in 1976 and 1977

rows.Name: Oklahoma City Butcher
rows.Notes: Killed and mutilated three women in Oklahoma City between 1976 and 1986

rows.Name: Phantom Killer
rows.Notes: Believed to have committed the Texarkana Moonlight Murders in Texas between February 23 and May 4, 1946

rows.Name: Pittsburg serial murders
rows.Notes: Single or multiple offenders who murdered one man and four women over three months in the city of Pittsburg, California

rows.Name: 1996 Raleigh murders
rows.Notes: Series of murders and rapes across the Raleigh, North Carolina area; multiple killers are suspected, including one who was convicted of two murders

rows.Name: Redhead murders
rows.Region where active: TN, AR , KY , MS , PA, WV
rows.Notes: Series of unsolved homicides believed to have been committed by an unidentified serial killer in Tennessee, Arkansas, Kentucky, Mississippi, Pennsylvania and West Virginia, also known as "The Bible Belt Strangler"

rows.Name: Sacramento Mad Killer
rows.Notes: Unidentified serial killer who murdered middle-aged men picked up from bars in the Sacramento area

rows.Name: San Diego serial murders
rows.Notes: Murders of women, predominantly prostitutes and drug addicts, across San Diego County . Initially believed to be a single serial killer, but later determined to be multiple killers.

rows.Name: Santa Rosa hitchhiker murders
rows.Notes: A series of at least seven unsolved homicides involving female hitchhikers that took place in Sonoma County and Santa Rosa of the North Bay area of California in 1972 and 1973

rows.Name: Servant Girl Annihilator
rows.Notes: Also known as the "Austin Axe Murderer"; responsible for at least seven murders and severe injuries to seven others in Austin, Texas between 1884 and 1885

rows.Name: Skid Row Stabber
rows.Notes: Murdered homeless men in Los Angeles' Skid Row neighborhood; Bobby Joe Maxwell was falsely convicted of two of the murders and accused of the rest, and died while in a coma prior to being exonerated

rows.Name: South Florida serial murders
rows.Notes: Murdered women, most of whom were homeless or prostitutes, primarily by strangling, four of the ten murders have been solved

rows.Name: South Memphis prostitute killings
rows.Notes: Murders of three sex workers in Memphis, Tennessee , in the winter of 2011; possibly linked to a fourth murder committed in 2015

rows.Name: Storyville Slayer
rows.Notes: Abducted, strangled and drowned predominantly female prostitutes around New Orleans ; thought to be multiple killers

rows.Name: Stockton serial shootings
rows.Notes: Shot one man to death in Oakland and five in Stockton and shot a woman in Stockton who survived her injuries. Wesley Brownlee was arrested for the murders on October 15, 2022.

rows.Name: Suitland murders
rows.Notes: Abducted, raped and stabbed to death women around Suitland, Maryland ; convicted murderer Alton Alonso Best is considered the prime suspect

rows.Name: Texas Killing Fields
rows.Notes: Since the early 1970s, roughly thirty bodies have been extracted from the fields, mainly consisting of young girls. As of March 2024, six of the cases have been definitively solved, and authorities now believe that multiple offenders are involved.

rows.Name: Tube Sock Killings
rows.Notes: Unsolved murders which occurred in the remote community of Mineral in Washington

rows.Name: Ventura Strangler
rows.Notes: Targeted sex workers in Ventura County, California , over several months in 1977; a suspect, Warren Alexander, was arrested in 2024

rows.Name: West Mesa murders
rows.Notes: Remains of eleven women, who disappeared between 2003 and 2005, found buried in the desert in Albuquerque, New Mexico, in 2009 and attributed to a bone collector

rows.Name: Zodiac Killer
rows.Notes: Targeted young couples. Remains unsolved but open in the California jurisdictions the five certain Zodiac murders occurred. Potentially thirty-seven total victims claimed but unverified.

table_name.additional_text: This list contains the following information:

rows.Description: Airport which handles both international and domestic traffic.
A civil enclave airport primarily used by Indian Armed Forces but has separate commercial terminal(s) to handle international and domestic traffic.

rows.No. overall: Similar to the other shorts episodes (particularly "Guest Directed Shorts"), this episode is composed of four shorts. 1) "Late Night, Black Light": After the lightbulb in the UG RV living room breaks, Uncle Grandpa plugs in a fluorescent lightbulb, and things get pretty crazy. 2) "I Love My Friends": Uncle Grandpa accidentally breaks a tire that a homeless cat was living in and the gang discuss what to do with him. 3) "Uncle Grandpa vs Mr. Gus": In this Batman vs. Superman spoof, Mr. Gus is ordered by the President to destroy Uncle Grandpa for being too funny, and an epic battle ensues. 4) "Good Morning": Uncle Grandpa says his signature catchphrase to everyone in the world. Note: The bumpers in this episode are directed by Rich Zim.

rows.Title: "Exquisite Grandpa"
rows.Written and storyboarded by: Pete Browngardt, Audie Harrison, Chris Allison, Andy Gonsalves, Myke Chilian, David Gemmill, Andres Salaff, Ryan Kramer, Nick Edwards, and Casey Alexander
rows.Story by: Kelsy Abbott and Pete Browngardt

rows.No. overall: Uncle Grandpa wakes up from a night terror, so he goes to "the one who knows all", who is a mustache man he finds on another planet. Before receiving his help to stop night terrors, he ends up telling him all the dreams he had leading up to the nightmare he woke up from. 1) "A Load of Laundry": An Uncle Grandpa from another planet arrives on Earth to sing a song about clean socks. 2) " The Tortoise and the Hare ": In the classic story of the race between the tortoise and the hare, Uncle Grandpa beats them and wins a trophy that turns out to awaken a genie that grants Uncle Grandpa three wishes. 3) "Tree Goblin": Uncle Grandpa and Mr. Gus sing the most annoying song ever to save Pizza Steve from a tree goblin. 4) "Save Hot Dog Person": Uncle Grandpa passes out in the desert after eating a horrible hot dog made by Evil Wizard, he then comes across Hot Dog Person, who is about to be eaten by birds. After a promise to get a hot dog from him, Uncle Grandpa runs off with him, but a change in him makes him throw Hot Dog Person to the birds. This turns out to be a simulation, in which Uncle Grandpa is told he failed. 5) "Uncle Grandpa Tea": Uncle Grandpa arrives to the Uncle Grandpa Tea he made his friends. Tiger, Mr. Gus, Pizza Steve, and Tiny Miracle are unsure about the tea, but after Uncle Grandpa finishes it, he uncovers a fortune telling him and his friends to "Make yourselves a sandwich.", he takes this literally and makes themselves into a sandwich for Ham Sandwich (from the 2008 pilot) to eat, where his nightmare left off. Note : Despite this episode being produced as the series finale , the following episode aired as the final episode.

Before receiving his help to stop night terrors, he ends up telling him all the dreams he had leading up to the nightmare he woke up from. 1) "A Load of Laundry": An Uncle Grandpa from another planet arrives on Earth to sing a song about clean socks. 2) " The Tortoise and the Hare ": In the classic story of the race between the tortoise and the hare, Uncle Grandpa beats them and wins a trophy that turns out to awaken a genie that grants Uncle Grandpa three wishes. 3) "Tree Goblin": Uncle Grandpa and Mr. Gus sing the most annoying song ever to save Pizza Steve from a tree goblin. 4) "Save Hot Dog Person": Uncle Grandpa passes out in the desert after eating a horrible hot dog made by Evil Wizard, he then comes across Hot Dog Person, who is about to be eaten by birds. After a promise to get a hot dog from him, Uncle Grandpa runs off with him, but a change in him makes him throw Hot Dog Person to the birds. This turns out to be a simulation, in which Uncle Grandpa is told he failed. 5) "Uncle Grandpa Tea": Uncle Grandpa arrives to the Uncle Grandpa Tea he made his friends. Tiger, Mr. Gus, Pizza Steve, and Tiny Miracle are unsure about the tea, but after Uncle Grandpa finishes it, he uncovers a fortune telling him and his friends to "Make yourselves a sandwich.", he takes this literally and makes themselves into a sandwich for Ham Sandwich (from the 2008 pilot) to eat, where his nightmare left off. Note : Despite this episode being produced as the series finale , the following episode aired as the final episode.

Officers pulled over 40-year old Valenzuela on a warrant for parole violation.  Valenzuela attempted to flee, which led to a foot chase during which Tasers were twice deployed unsuccessfully.  After catching up to him, a struggle ensued during which one of the officers is heard saying "I'm going to (expletive) choke you out".  The officer "knelt down on his neck until he became unresponsive"  after which paramedics were called in an attempt to revive him, but he was pronounced dead at the scene.

rows.Title: Centuries ago, people in warmer parts of the earth believed that a dread disease was contracted from unhealthy air generated in swamps. From this belief came the word "malaria," which means " bad air ". The word is still used to describe a parasitic disease that remains one of the world's major public health problems. Efforts to find and isolate the causes of malaria make one of the greatest scientific detective stories of all time. Mosquitoes of the genus Anopheles were found to be implicated. But so far, their control is far from accomplished. Program features Dr. A. Murray Fallis, parasitologist with the Ontario Research Foundation and professor at the University of Toronto . Host is Lister Sinclair .

rows.Title: It was not until 1930 that the outside world knew that there were people living in the highlands of Papua, New Guinea. In 1950 the first contact was made with a group of 55,000 Mendi, part of a million inhabitants of the New Guinea highlands, formerly not known to exist. The Australians have since built an airstrip, a hospital, schools, a hotel and other permanent buildings there, but the Mendi have kept their culture intact. A CBC film crew directed by Nancy Archibald has recorded some of the ancient culture and lifestyle of the Mendi and the results are presented in this special one-hour documentary.

rows.Title: The Australian Broadcasting Corporation produced four half-hour films about the Macquarie Islands. This episode of The Nature of Things compiles two of them. The first was originally entitled 'Man the Hunter, Man the Keeper.' The second was originally entitled 'The Dominant Male.' We now understand the importance of wetlands to our watersheds, but this has not always been the case. Vanishing Wetlands describes how almost all of the wetlands in Europe and North America have been drained and filled to make way for industrial development and agriculture. The viewer learns about the water cycle and how wetlands reduce the severity of floods by storing excess water during flooding events, how wetlands act as filters and allow sediment to settle before reaching waterways, how a wetland is utilized by both aquatic and terrestrial species, and the importance of wetlands to migratory birds.

The Edge of Eden: Living with Grizzlies (previously broadcast in abbreviated form as The Bear Man of Kamchatka ) tracks Canadian bear expert Charlie Russell as he rescues two orphaned cubs destined for death in a squalid Russian zoo. Charlie becomes their surrogate mother and shows them the lay of the land in their new home territory; what plants to eat, how to catch fish and how to escape from predatory male bears. In a world where "might makes right" and aggression becomes the only way to deal with conflicts, Charlie Russell is proving that it is possible to live peacefully with one of the world's most feared and misunderstood creatures.

rows.Title: How smart are animals? Traditionally, we've answered that question by comparing them to us. rows.Title: Cracking Cancer follows a group of patients, all with incurable cancer, through a highly experimental clinical trial at the BC Cancer Agency . The research team then searches to find which drug, of all available drugs, might block that growth factor. The results have been quite promising.

rows.Name: St John's Anglican Church
rows.Description and significance: St John's Church is the oldest surviving public building within Canberra's city precinct, predating the establishment of the capital by almost 70 years. The Schoolhouse Museum within the church precinct displays items dating back to Canberra's rural past.
rows.Preservation and access: The church building and surrounding precinct remains an active place of worship and Canberra landmark.

rows.Name: Blundells Cottage
rows.Description and significance: Blundells Cottage is five room stone cottage, and is one of the few reminders of the rural history of Canberra left in the city.
rows.Preservation and access: The building is listed by the National Trust of Australia and operates as a museum.

rows.Name: Canberry, Kanberry
rows.Description and significance: Canberry was the first building in the ACT .
rows.Preservation and access: Canberry was knocked down in 1942 to make way for the construction of the Royal Canberra Hospital .

rows.Name: Tharwa Bridge
rows.Description and significance: Tharwa Bridge was the first bridge built across the Murrumbidgee River .
rows.Preservation and access: The four span Allan truss bridge is still open to traffic. (Closed in 2006 - temporarily) The bridge reopened in August 2008 to light traffic, below 5 tonnes .

rows.Name: Yarralumla
rows.Description and significance: Built by the Campbell family, the house became the home of the Governor-General of Australia from 1927.

rows.Name: Duntroon House
rows.Description and significance: Built by the Campbell family, now the officer's mess at RMC Duntroon . The oldest surviving private building in Canberra.

table_name.header_chain: List of Ukrainian Baroque stone churches > Ukraine > Chernihiv Oblast

rows.Name: Cathedral of the Life-Giving Trinity
rows.Notes: Five-dome church. Built at the expense of Ivan Samoylovych and expanded at the expense of Ivan Mazepa . Burnt down on 13 November 1708 during the Sack of Baturyn .  Another wooden church with the same name was later built in a different place and closed in 1787.

rows.Name: Annunciation Church
rows.Notes: Cruciform nine-part one-dome church. Destroyed in the Soviet period.

rows.Name: Trinity Cathedral
rows.Notes: Five-part one-dome church. Destroyed in 1967.

rows.Name: Boris and Gleb Cathedral
rows.Notes: The medieval church was rebuilt at the expense of Ivan Mazepa. The two-story bell tower that was built in the 1670s was destroyed in the 1960s when the medieval look was returned to the cathedral.

rows.Name: Church of All Saints in the Chernihiv Collegium
rows.Notes: Built by Ivan Mazepa. Two-story church with a narrow bell tower on top. The decor features elements of the Naryshkin Baroque.

rows.Name: Church of the Presentation of the Virgin Mary of the Trinity Monastery
rows.Notes: Two-dome refectory church with a rectangular altar section and exterior features of Moscow Baroque. Its 18th-century iconostasis was built by the order of Ivan Mazepa.

rows.Name: Dormition Cathedral  of Yelets Dormition Monastery
rows.Notes: The medieval church was rebuilt by Theodosius of Chernihiv  and Ioanikiy (Galyatovsky)  at the expense of numerous noble families, including the Lyzohubs and the Baryatynskys. Three cupolas were added above the narthex (of which two have been preserved), and one more above the altar. It was expanded in 1689. The bell tower was built in 1670–1675. The iconostasis was made in 1669–1670 and lost in the 1920s.

rows.Name: Piatnytska Church
rows.Notes: The medieval church was rebuilt in the Baroque style. It was greatly damaged during World War II, and consequently reconstructed by Pyotr Baranovsky to its 13th-century appearance.

rows.Name: St. Catherine's Church
rows.Notes: Cruciform nine-part five-dome church. Built at the expense of the Lyzohub family. The iconostasis was destroyed in the Soviet period.

rows.Name: St. Elijah Church of the Trinity Monastery
rows.Notes: The medieval one-dome church was rebuilt on the exterior, with added domes above the narthex and the apse . The two-story bell tower was built later. The iconostasis was made in the 1770s.

rows.Name: Saints Peter and Paul Church of Yelets Dormition Monastery
rows.Notes: Refectory church. Lost its original appearance when it was rebuilt in the end of the 18th century.

rows.Name: Holy Trinity Cathedral of the Trinity Monastery
rows.Notes: Originally built by Lazar Baranovych , since 1688 by Ivan Baptista at the expense of Ivan Mazepa, and later by a group headed by Osip Startsev . It was a large three-nave seven-dome church until four of its domes were destroyed. The cathedral was reconstructed in the 1980s–1990s. The seven-tier iconostasis of 1695 was destroyed in the Soviet period.

rows.Name: St. George's Cathedral  of Danivka Monastery
rows.Notes: Three-part three-dome three-apse church.

rows.Name: Intercession Church
rows.Notes: Five-part five-dome church in with features similar to Naryshkin Baroque. Built at the expense of Ivan Mazepa. It was heavily damaged during World War II, and partially disassembled. The church is being reconstructed.

rows.Name: Dormition Church of the Hustynia Monastery
rows.Notes: Cruciform one-dome refectory church. Built by Ivan Mazepa.

rows.Name: St. Nicholas the Wondermaker Church of the Hustynia Monastery
rows.Notes: Gate church, fully rebuilt in the 19th century. Only the lower parts of the current building preserve the original structure.

rows.Name: Sts. Peter and Paul Church of the Hustynia Monastery
rows.Notes: Cruciform nine-part five-dome gate church.

rows.Name: Trinity Cathedral of the Hustynia Monastery
rows.Notes: Cruciform nine-part five-dome church built at the expense of Ivan Samoylovych. The 18th-century five-tier iconostasis was destroyed in the Soviet period.

rows.Name: Cathedral of the Nativity of Virgin Mary
rows.Notes: Large five-dome church with elements of Elizabethan Baroque. Built by Andrey Kvasov and Ivan Grigorovich-Barsky at the expense of Natalia Rozumovska  . The four-story bell tower was built together with the cathedral. The iconostasis was made in the 1760s.

rows.Name: St. Nicholas Church
rows.Notes: Cruciform one-dome three-apse church. Built by Kyrylo Tarakh-Tarlovsky  .

rows.Name: Intercession Church of Ladan Monastery
rows.Notes: Three-part three-dome church with a separate bell tower built in 19th century. The cathedral was distorted and the bell tower was destroyed in the Soviet period. The cathedral is being reconstructed.

rows.Name: Transfiguration (Trinity) Cathedral of Maksaky Monastery
rows.Notes: Three-nave one-dome (three-dome after 17th century) church with elements of Belarusian Baroque. Established by Adam Kisiel . Destroyed in the late 1940s.

rows.Name: Presentation of the Virgin Mary Church of Maksaky Monastery
rows.Notes: One-dome refectory church. Destroyed in the 1930s.

rows.Name: Annunciation Cathedral  of the Annunciation Monastery
rows.Notes: Large five-dome church with influence of Russian Baroque by G. Ustinov. The façades were rebuilt in the 19th century in the classicist style.

rows.Name: Church of John the Apostle
rows.Notes: Two-story one-dome church. Belongs to the tetraconch type.

rows.Name: Epiphany Church
rows.Notes: Rebuilt, distorted in the Soviet period.

rows.Name: Holy Exaltation of the Cross Church
rows.Notes: One-dome church. Houses the tomb of Petro Rozumovsky. The winter church and the bell tower were built in 1860.

rows.Name: Intercession Church
rows.Notes: One-dome tetrachonch church. The bell tower was built in the 19th century.

rows.Name: Presentation of the Virgin Mary Church of the Presentation of the Virgin Mary Monastery
rows.Notes: One-dome church. The bell tower was built in the 19th century.

rows.Name: St. Michael's Church
rows.Notes: Small three-part one-dome church. One of the three Greek churches of Nizhyn.

rows.Name: St. Nicholas Cathedral
rows.Notes: Large cruciform nine-part five-dome church. Much of the exterior decoration has been reconstructed hypothetically. It iconostasis was made in the 1730s and destroyed in the Soviet period.  This church is the prototype of Ukrainian Baroque cruciform five-dome churches.

rows.Name: Sts. Pantaleon and Basil Church
rows.Notes: Three-part one-dome church.

rows.Name: Transfiguration Church
rows.Notes: Cruciform three-dome church. It was heavily damaged during World War II, and is currently under reconstruction.

rows.Name: Trinity Church
rows.Notes: Small cruciform one-dome church. Gained classicist features in the 1830s. One of the three Greek churches of Nizhyn.

rows.Name: Dormition Cathedral
rows.Notes: Nine-part five-dome church. The bell tower was built in the 19th century.

rows.Name: Exaltation of the Cross Church
rows.Notes: Three-part one-dome church with elements of Petrine Baroque . Destroyed in the 1930s.

rows.Name: Resurrection Church
rows.Notes: Originally a three-part one-dome church. Rebuilt, and finally destroyed in the 1930s.

rows.Name: Sts. Peter and Paul Church  of the Transfiguration Monastery
rows.Notes: Cruciform one-dome refectory church.

rows.Name: Transfiguration Cathedral of the Transfiguration Monastery
rows.Notes: The medieval church was rebuilt into the Ukrainian Baroque style. It was disassembled and a new classicist church with a design by Giacomo Quarenghi was built in its place in 1791–1806.

rows.Name: Cathedral of St. Nicholas the Wondermaker of Krupytskyi Monastery
rows.Notes: Cruciform nine-part five-dome church. Built at the expense of Ivan Domontovych  . Destroyed in the 1930s together with its 18th-century five-tier iconostasis.

rows.Name: St. Michael's Church
rows.Notes: Originally a three-part one-dome church. Built at the expense of Oleksandr Shylo. Two more domes were built in the 1760s–1770s above the narthex and the apse.

rows.Name: St. Nicholas Church
rows.Notes: Hall church with an elongated sanctuary and a bell tower. Built at the expense of the polkovnyk Hnat Galagan  .

rows.Name: Transfiguration Cathedral
rows.Notes: Nine-part five-dome church. Built at the expense of Hnat Galagan.

rows.Name: Cathedral of St. Nicholas the Wondermaker of Rykhly Monastery
rows.Notes: Cruciform nine-part five-dome church with a large central dome. Built at the expense of the brigadiers F. Kachenovsky and P. Chyzhevsky. Destroyed in 1930.

rows.Name: Church of St. Nicholas the Wondermaker of Rykhly Monastery
rows.Notes: Small three-part one-dome church. Built at the expense of F. Kachenovsky and P. Chyzhevsky. Destroyed in the 1930s.

rows.Name: Church of the Nativity of John the Baptist of Rykhly Monastery
rows.Notes: Five-part three-dome gate church with elements of Elizabethan Baroque. Destroyed in the 1930s.

rows.Name: Resurrection Church
rows.Notes: Cruciform nine-part one-dome church. Built by Yakiv Lyzohub . The bell tower was built in the 19th century.

rows.Name: Resurrection Church
rows.Notes: Five-part three-dome church with Provincial Baroque façades. Destroyed in the 1930s.

rows.Name: Trinity Church
rows.Notes: Three-part three-dome church with elements of Naryshkin Baroque. Built at the expense of the merchant Hryhoriy Korenko. Destroyed in the 1950s.

table_name.header_chain: List of Ukrainian Baroque stone churches > Ukraine > Kharkiv Oblast

rows.Name: Dormition Church
rows.Notes: One-dome church with a separate bell tower. Destroyed intentionally in 1948.

rows.Name: Transfiguration Cathedral
rows.Notes: Five-part five-dome church. Distorted by construction in 1902–1903, but subsequently restored to original form in the 1950s. The iconostasis made in 1765 was destroyed in the Soviet period.

rows.Name: Church of the Nativity of Jesus
rows.Notes: Five-part five-dome church with elements of Provincial Baroque. It was expanded in the 19th century and destroyed the Soviet period.

rows.Name: Intercession Cathedral of the Intercession Monastery
rows.Notes: Two-story three-part three-dome church with a tent-roofed bell tower.

rows.Name: St. Nicholas the Wondermaker Church
rows.Notes: Three-part three-dome church with features of Naryshkin Baroque. Destroyed in 1886.

rows.Name: Trinity Church
rows.Notes: Small three-part two-dome church with a separate bell tower. Combined features of Ukrainian and Naryshkin Baroque styles. It was destroyed in the 1850s and replaced by a new church  designed by Konstantin Thon .

rows.Name: Ascension Cathedral of Khorosheve Monastery
rows.Notes: Three-part three-dome church. Expanded to a five-part five-dome church in 1835–1837. Included features of Moscow Baroque. Destroyed in the Soviet period.

rows.Name: St. George's Church of Kuriazhanka Monastery
rows.Notes: Two-story one-dome refectory church. Destroyed in the Soviet period  when the monastery was turned into the Kuriazhanka Corrective Colony  .

rows.Name: St. Onuphrius Church of Kuriazhanka Monastery
rows.Notes: Cruciform one-dome church. Destroyed in the Soviet period.

rows.Name: Transfiguration Cathedral of Kuriazhanka Monastery
rows.Notes: Five-dome (after 19th century — three-dome) church. Partially ruined in the Soviet period and not restored since. Its 18th-century bell tower was destroyed.

rows.Name: Intercession Church
rows.Notes: Three-part church with one two-story dome. Destroyed in the Soviet period.

table_name.header_chain: List of Ukrainian Baroque stone churches > Ukraine > Kyiv Oblast

rows.Name: Dormition Church
rows.Notes: Three-part one-dome church with later additions. A separate tent-roofed bell tower was located nearby. The church and the bell tower were destroyed in the 1930s.

rows.Name: St. Nicholas Church
rows.Notes: Originally a large three-throne church. A part of the church was destroyed.

rows.Name: Transfiguration Church of the Transfiguration Monastery
rows.Notes: One-dome rectangular church.

rows.Name: Sts. Peter and Paul Church of Mezhyhirya Monastery
rows.Notes: Two-story one-dome refectory church with a three-story bell tower on its western side. Built by Ivan Grigorovich-Barsky and Petro Kalnyshevsky .  Combined features of Ukrainian and Elizabethan baroque styles. Ruined in 1936.

rows.Name: Transfiguration Cathedral of Mezhyhirya Monastery
rows.Notes: Built by Patriarch Joachim . Originally a large six-column five-dome church. In 1810s it was rebuilt in the classicist style.  Ruined in 1936.

rows.Name: Ascension Cathedral of the Ascension Monastery
rows.Notes: Large cruciform nine-part one-dome church. Built at the expense of Ivan Mazepa. The three-story bell tower was built in the second half of the 18th century.

rows.Name: Intercession Church
rows.Notes: Seven-part three-dome church. Built at the expense of Ivan Myrovych  . Destroyed in the Soviet period.

rows.Name: St. Michael's Church
rows.Notes: Built on the place of a previous wooden church. The monastery complex was damaged during World War II. Murals from 18th–19th centuries have been preserved on the inside. The bell tower was built in 1747.

rows.Name: Intercession Church
rows.Notes: Possibly the oldest church of the traditional Ukrainian Baroque composition. Three-part one-dome church with a bell tower that was built later. Built by Ivan Sulyma .

rows.Name: Sts. Anthony and Theodosius Cathedral
rows.Notes: Large five-nave five-dome church with elements of Elizabethan Baroque. Built by Stepan Kovnir.

table_name.header_chain: List of Ukrainian Baroque stone churches > Ukraine > Poltava Oblast

rows.Name: Dormition Church
rows.Notes: Cruciform nine-part five-dome church built at the expense of Mykhailo Borokhovych  .  The five-tier iconostasis was lost in the 1930s. The church itself collapsed in 1973, and its ruins were disassembled.

rows.Name: Transfiguration Cathedral  of Mhar Monastery
rows.Notes: Built at the expense of Ivan Samoylovych and Ivan Mazepa. Large three-nave church, originally with seven domes, and since the 18th century — with five. Its bell tower was built in 1785. The iconostasis that was made in 1762–1765 was destroyed in the Soviet period.

rows.Name: Ascension Church  of Pushkarivka Monastery
rows.Notes: Towerless tetraconch church. Neglected in the Soviet period and reconstructed in the 2000s.

rows.Name: Dormition Cathedral
rows.Notes: Three-nave five-dome church with additions from the 19th century. The classicist bell tower was built in 1776–1801. The cathedral was destroyed in 1938.  The cathedral was rebuilt in the 1990s with significant violations of design documentation.

rows.Name: Holy Cross Exaltation Cathedral of the Holy Cross Exaltation Monastery
rows.Notes: Large three-nave seven-dome church built by the Kochubey family . The bell tower was built in 1786. Decorations and the four-tier iconostasis form 1772 were destroyed in the Soviet period.

rows.Name: Trinity Church of the Holy Cross Exaltation Monastery
rows.Notes: One-dome refectory church. Partially rebuilt.

rows.Name: Cathedral of the Nativity of the Blessed Virgin Mary
rows.Notes: Small three-part church. Built by order of the regimental osavul A. M. Ilchenko.

rows.Name: Transfiguration Church
rows.Notes: Cruciform nine-part five-dome church (before the 19th century — nine-dome). Built by Stepan Kovnir at the expense of Danylo Apostol . The five-tier iconostasis was made in the 1730s. Functions as the tomb of the hetman and his family.

table_name.header_chain: List of Ukrainian Baroque stone churches > Ukraine > Sumy Oblast

rows.Name: St. Michael's Church of Hlukhiv Peter and Paul Monastery
rows.Notes: Three-part three-dome gate church. The dome above the narthex was disassembled in the end of 18th century, and a bell tower was built in its place. The church was slowly taken apart for materials after World War II until almost nothing remained.

rows.Name: Sts. Peter and Paul Church of Hlukhiv Peter and Paul Monastery
rows.Notes: Three-part three-dome church with Naryshkin Baroque decor. Built by M. Yefimov on the order of Demetrius of Rostov . Destroyed in the 1930s.

rows.Name: Trinity Cathedral of Okhtyrka Trinity Monastery
rows.Notes: Three-part three-dome church with Naryshkin Baroque influence. Built at the expense of T. Nadarzhynsky. Partially rebuilt in 1842, and the bell tower was constructed in 18th–19th centuries. Heavily damaged during World War II and consequently taken apart for materials (except for the bell tower).

rows.Name: Cathedral of the Nativity of Virgin Mary of Hamaliivka St. Charalambos Monastery
rows.Notes: Cruciform nine-part five-dome church. Built at the expense of Ivan Skoropadsky. The bell tower built in 18th–19th centuries was destroyed in the 1960s.

rows.Name: St. Charalambos Church of Hamaliivka St. Charalambos Monastery
rows.Notes: Small refectory church. Distorted in the Soviet period and not restored. The church used to house the tomb of the Skoropadsky family .

rows.Name: Church of the Nativity of Blessed Virgin Mary at Veryhine
rows.Notes: Three-part three-dome church. Its three-story bell tower was built in 1803. The church and the bell tower were destroyed in the 1930s.

rows.Name: St. Anastasia Church
rows.Notes: Small church with no domes. Built at the expense of Ivan Skoropadsky . Destroyed in 1896.

rows.Name: St. Michael's Church
rows.Notes: Built by M. Yefimov. Destroyed by a fire in 1784.

rows.Name: St. Nicholas Church
rows.Notes: Two-part two-dome church with Naryshkin Baroque influence. Built by V. Yalotsky. The narthex and bell tower were built in 19th century. The 18th-century five-tier iconostasis was destroyed in the Soviet period.

rows.Name: Three Holy Hierarchs Church
rows.Notes: Cruciform three-part one-dome church. Destroyed in the 1930s.

rows.Name: Trinity Cathedral
rows.Notes: Large cruciform three-dome church with elements of late Baroque and Classicism. Built by Ivan Skoropadsky, with additions by Andrey Kvasov and others. The classicist bell tower was destroyed in 1929, while the cathedral was destroyed in 1962.

rows.Name: Cathedral of the Nativity of Virgin Mary
rows.Notes: Three-part one-dome church. Built at the expense of H. Nizhynsky and I. Vakulenko. Rebuilt in Neo-Byzantine style in 1886. Destroyed in the 1930s.

rows.Name: Cathedral of the Nativity of Virgin Mary
rows.Notes: Three-part three-dome church. Built at the expense of sotnyk H. Ohiievsky and priest Y. Makovsky. The bell tower was built in 1829–1830, and later additions date to the 19th century. Destroyed in the Soviet period.

rows.Name: Dormition Cathedral
rows.Notes: Two-story church with classicist elements. The lower church is four-columned, and the upper part is three-part and three-dome. The classicist bell tower was built in the 19th century. The cathedral and the bell tower were destroyed in 1939.

rows.Name: Dormition Church
rows.Notes: Cruciform one-dome church with a narthex. The building was somewhat damaged and the iconostasis from the 1770s was destroyed in the Soviet period.

rows.Name: Dormition Cathedral
rows.Notes: Four-column church with one dome. The bell tower is from the 19th century. Destroyed in the Soviet period.

rows.Name: Intercession Cathedral
rows.Notes: Large three-part three-dome church. Combines elements of Ukrainian and Elizabethan Baroque. Designed by D. Ukhtomsky and S. Dudynsky. The bell tower was buit in the 1770s.

rows.Name: St. Nicholas Cossack Church
rows.Notes: Two-story three-part church. The bell tower was built in 1770.

rows.Name: Holy Spirit Cathedral
rows.Notes: Three-part three-dome church.

rows.Name: St. Nicholas Church
rows.Notes: Three-part one-dome church with a two-story bell tower. Destroyed in the 1930s.

rows.Name: Intercession Church
rows.Notes: Seven-part three-dome church with Baroque and Classicist elements. The classicist bell tower was consecrated in 1821. The church and the bell tower were destroyed in the Soviet period.

rows.Name: Resurrection Cathedral
rows.Notes: Two-story three-part three-dome church with Naryshkin Baroque decor. The original tent-roofed bell tower has not been preserved. The current bell tower was built in 20th century and imitated the cathedral's style.

rows.Name: St. Michael's Church
rows.Notes: Cruciform one-dome church with a three-story bell tower.

rows.Name: Transfiguration Church
rows.Notes: Three-part three-dome church that combines Ukrainian and Elizabethan Baroque styles.

table_name.header_chain: List of Ukrainian Baroque stone churches > Russia

rows.Name: Church of St. Basil the Great
rows.Notes: Original-style church without columns. Served as the winter church next to the city's Transfiguration Cathedral. Demolished in the Soviet period.

rows.Name: Dormition Cathedral
rows.Notes: Large nine-part nine-dome church with a classicist bell tower. Destroyed in the Soviet period.

rows.Name: St. Nicholas Cathedral of Katashin Monastery
rows.Notes: Four-column five-dome three-apse church. Built at the expense of Mykhailo Myklashevsky  modeled after Mazepa's churches in Kyiv. Almost completely destroyed in 1960.

rows.Name: Church of Virgin Mary of the Sign
rows.Notes: Three-part three-dome church built by the boyar Aleksei Shein .  The bell tower and the iconostasis were built in the 18th century. The church was destroyed in 1936.

rows.Name: Church of Virgin Mary of Kazan in Uzkoye
rows.Notes: Cruciform five-dome church with Naryshkin Baroque decor. Built by the boyar T. Streshnyov. The 17th-century iconostasis was destroyed in the Soviet period.

rows.Name: Church of the Nativity of the Blessed Virgin Mary
rows.Notes: Nine-part one-dome church with elements of Classicism. Built at the expense of Y. Myklashevska.

rows.Name: Resurrection Military Cathedral
rows.Notes: Large nine-part nine-dome church. The two-story parvise and tent-roofed bell tower were built in 1725–1730. The iconostasis was made in 1749.

rows.Name: Cathedral of the Nativity of Christ
rows.Notes: Three-part three-dome church. The interior decor has not been preserved.

rows.Name: Epiphany Church
rows.Notes: Cubic one-dome one-apse church with 19th-century extensions.

rows.Name: Transfiguration Church
rows.Notes: Three-part seven-dome church. Destroyed in the Soviet period.

rows.Name: Epiphany Church
rows.Notes: Three-part two-dome church with a tent-roofed bell tower. Combines features of Ukrainian and Naryshkin Baroque. Destroyed (likely in the 1930s).

rows.Name: Intercession Cathedral
rows.Notes: Cruciform one-dome refectory church. The Classicist bell tower was built in the 1790s.

rows.Name: Church of Forty Martyrs of Sebaste of the Trinity Monastery
rows.Notes: Small two-dome refectory church. Entirely destroyed in the 1940s.  Siberian Baroque style with strong influence of Ukrainian Baroque.

rows.Name: Sts. Peter and Paul Church of the Trinity Monastery
rows.Notes: Cruciform five-dome church with later additions (including a tent-roofed bell tower).  Siberian Baroque style with strong influence of Ukrainian Baroque.

rows.Name: Trinity Cathedral of the Trinity Monastery
rows.Notes: Three-part four-column five-dome church with later additions.  Siberian Baroque style with strong influence of Ukrainian Baroque.

rows.Name: Annunciation Cathedral  of the Mitrophan Monastery
rows.Notes: Large five-part five-dome church. Distorted after it was rebuilt in the 19th century. Heavily damaged during World War II and subsequently disassembled in the 1950s.

rows.Name: Dormition Cathedral of Kamenka Assumption Monastery
rows.Notes: Seven-part one-dome church. Rebuilt in the 19th century. It is currently in a severely damaged state: the vaults and the upper part of the dome have collapsed, and a significant part of the exterior decoration has been destroyed. It has not been restored.

table_name.header_chain: List of killings by law enforcement officers in the United States in the 1950s > 1950s
table_name.additional_text: The table below lists 111 people.

rows.Description: Pickett was beaten by a police officer while in a jail cell and died from his injuries two days later.
Taylor and his compatriot, Victor Wayne Whitley, ran a police roadblock and were fired on by police.  Taylor was killed by officer Lester Kenan.  Whitley escaped and was captured the next day.

Nader was killed with Michael Burke during a police ambush of a supermarket burglary. Burke and Nader, whom police had suspected of "safecracking" in the area, broke into the supermarket, encountered police, and ran. Police opened fire and killed Burke immediately.  Nader returned police fire and was shot to death by police.  Over 100 shots were fired in the exchange.
Burke was shot to death while running from police during an ambush of a supermarket burglary.

Wilson killed his two sisters-in-law and another woman in June 1956.  He was sought by police for 11 days until a tip alerted them to his location.  He refused to surrender when ordered to by police and was subsequently shot twice in the head by patrolman Russell Duffy.

Rollins was held under siege by over 200 police officers in the home of his nephew, Bernard Smith.  After a tear gas bomb set the house on fire Rollins ran out firing a shotgun and was killed as ten officers fired over 40 shots at him.  Smith later said of Rollins that "He read the Bible some, but mostly he rode a bicycle up and down the sidewalk when he wasn't working.  He never talked to adults in the family.  He only smiled."

Tommie Woods, a Black elderly farmer, was killed by Sheriff J. O. Walker and Deputy Sheriff Ed Potter. While federal authorities concluded the killing of Woods was "wanton and unnecessary", the case was closed because the variation between eyewitness accounts  "would prove to be too difficult to overcome if they prosecuted."

Leonard Morisson, a Black veteran, was killed by Fort Worth police after the police were called to settle a disturbance outside his home. Morrison was shot in the back and died in hospital three days later.

Della McDuffie, a Black housewife, was beaten to death by police in a cafe she owned with her husband. She used a wheelchair and was unable to escape. A year later, her husband was found dead under suspicious circumstances.

Noel was one of 1,600 prisoners rioting in an Ohio penitentiary.  Twenty-one Ohio highway patrolmen were trapped inside the prison and opened fire with shotguns on a crowd of prisoners.  Four, including Noel, were wounded, and Noel died of his wounds.

Kauffman abducted his own two-year-old son, another man, and the man's two-year-old son after shooting his estranged wife in the arm.  He drove himself and his three hostages to his own house.  When he was forced outside by tear gas, he attempted to flee in his car but was fired on by officers.  When Kauffman returned fire he was shot to death by police, whose gunfire also wounded Kauffman's son in the head.

Shot and killed by county sheriff Willis V. McCall while being transported from the Florida State Prison in Raiford .  Shepherd was handcuffed to Walter Irvin .  McCall claimed that the prisoners attacked him when he had to stop the car to change a flat tire, although Irvin's testimony and voluminous evidence made McCall's version implausible.
Willie Ruth Moseley, a Black pregnant 17-year-old, was killed by police officer Floyd Vinyard, who was not prosecuted.

Arthur Collins, a Black WWII veteran, was killed by Highway Patrol Sergeant W. A. Norris during a standoff with multiple police officers. Collins was possibly suffering from a mental illness and was allegedly threatening his family and neighborhood with a rifle.
Willie Carlisle, a Black service station employee, was beaten to death by two police officers who accused him of letting the air out of a police car tire.
