table_name.header_chain: List of museums with Soap Box Derby racers > Museums with Soap Box Derby racers
table_name.additional_text: Below is a list of various museums and historical institutions as well as venues open to the public that have in the past or are currently exhibiting Soap Box Derby racers or adding them to their permanent collections, usually acquired via donation by the cars' original owners.

rows.Name: 1910 Franklin County Garage & Auto Museum
rows.Notes: Has a single Derby car, named "Rythm Ride," on exhibit on the showroom floor.

rows.Name: 52nd International Old Opel IG Annual Meeting
rows.Notes: The city of Troisdorf hosted the 52nd gathering of historic Opel vehicles and their enthusiasts from all over Europe to an open-air exhibit near the Troisdorf Town Hall.   Exhibited was an Opel-era German Derby racer alongside other artifacts manufactured by Opel AG .

rows.Name: 54th Street Grill and Bar
rows.Notes: This restaurant chain has two locations with a Derby car on display in each, located in Blue Springs, Missouri  and Edwardsville, Illinois.

rows.Name: Aberdeen Museum of History
rows.Notes: Has two 1960s cars on exhibit, both piloted by Ed Gegen, located in its hot rod garage diorama.

rows.Name: Akron History Center
rows.Notes: Opening 15 April 2025 to the public,  the nascent Akron History Center  hosts artifacts from Akron's extensive 200-year history,  including a Derby car (pictured) piloted by 1948 World Champion Donald Strub (1934–2020).  Pictured in 2016 at the Soap Box Derby Hall of Fame Museum at Derby Downs , the extant car is found suspended over the central staircase.

rows.Name: Albany Regional Museum
rows.Notes: Hosted an exhibit in 2023 titled Hub City , which featured in the children's area a transportation-themed display comprising two Derby cars that visiting kids could climb into.   Among them was a racer piloted by 2010 Super Stock World Champion Tucker McClaran.   Another car piloted by Allen Blake, who competed as a class A entry in Salem, OR in 1953  and 1954,  is exhibited as well.

rows.Name: Allen County Museum and Historical Society
rows.Notes: Has a racer (illustration pictured) from 1971 Lima, Ohio Champion James Ethan Jackson.   The car is not on public display.

rows.Name: Allegheny Museum
rows.Notes: Has a racer  piloted by 1949 Cumberland, Maryland Champion Neil Jones, donated in 2015  and exhibited the same year.

rows.Name: All Sports Museum of Southern New Jersey
rows.Notes: Has a collection of Derby memorabilia,   including a racer (illustration pictured) piloted by Marvin Rammel (1927—2024),  who competed in the Bridgeton, New Jersey local race in 1940.  Rammel had the car restored to its original red and sponsor livery, and donated it to the Museum in 1991.

rows.Name: America on Wheels Auto Museum
rows.Notes: Hosted an exhibit (pictured) of numerous Derby cars.

rows.Name: American Treasure Tour Museum
rows.Notes: Has on exhibit a few Derby cars, including a blue class A entry from New Castle, Pennsylvania piloted by Ronnie Boy,   who won the Best Constructed Award in 1970.

rows.Name: Anderson County Museum
rows.Notes: Hosts an exhibit with a 1940 Derby car  said to be from the community, along with a helmet and race jersey from 1941 Anderson Champ Joseph E. Harbin displayed above.

rows.Name: Antique Automobile Club of America, or AACA
rows.Notes: Exhibited two cars piloted by 1971 York, Pennsylvania Champion Glenn Dale Laughman and 1972 York, Pennsylvania Champion Debbie Laughman.

rows.Name: Aroma Guesthouse
rows.Notes: A tourist accommodation on the Danish Baltic Sea island of Ærø in SE Denmark, the guesthouse has in their Tintin guest room a post Opel-era German Derby racer hung decoratively on the wall.

rows.Name: The Bag Factory
rows.Notes: A retail facility in an historic property has a Derby car piloted by 1994 Goshen Masters Rally Champion Greg Koop  suspended above the retail floor.

rows.Name: Beaver Falls Historical Society Museum
rows.Notes: Exhibited a racer (illustration pictured) piloted by 1969 Beaver Falls Champion Robert Javens.

rows.Name: Beech Creek/Marsh Creek Watershed Heritage Museum
rows.Notes: Has a 1963 class A racer donated in 2019 by builder/owner Steve Rhoads.

rows.Name: Behringer-Crawford Museum
rows.Notes: Located in the Roads Gallery on the second level of the museum is an artistically-painted Derby car named Lucky Lisa ,   which was piloted by Cincinnati, Ohio entrant Lisa Luthy.  The car received Best Upholstered distinction in 1972.

rows.Name: Belfast Historical Society and Museum
rows.Notes: Has a car (illustration pictured) piloted by Belfast, Maine class B racer Butch Richards, who competed in 1966 and 1967 in the Bangor, Maine statewide Derby race. Donated to the museum in 2022 it was announced that it would be put on display in the near future.

rows.Name: Big Putts Mini Golf
rows.Notes: Has at this family-oriented recreational facility an interactive display of a red laydown Derby car   that was piloted by 1977 Racine, Wisconsin Champion Rob Lemerond.

rows.Name: Blackstone's Smokehouse
rows.Notes: Has a car piloted by 1957 Flint, MI Champion Dwight Harley Polzin. The racer is suspended above the restaurant floor.

rows.Name: Boone County Museum of History
rows.Notes: Has two cars on exhibit piloted in 1963 by Dale Drake  and Allen Graves.   Drake won runner-up the year prior in Belvidere, as well as receiving the best-engineered award for his car.

rows.Name: Cape Fear Museum of History and Science
rows.Notes: Had as recent as 2011 a class A racer in their collection not on display.

rows.Name: Carillon Historical Park
rows.Notes: Has two Derby cars on display in the "Toys Manufactured in Dayton, Ohio" exhibit of the Heritage Center of Dayton Manufacturing & Entrepreneurship in Carillon Park. The first is a racer suspended from the ceiling   once piloted by Donald Doerfert, who placed third in Dayton in 1934 and won the Best Constructed trophy.  The second is a blue racer   (illustration pictured) piloted by Cuyahoga Falls, Ohio entrant Dave Welty. Competing from 1946 until 1951, Welty made it to the third round of the Beacon Journal-sponsored local race in Akron, Ohio in 1949.

rows.Name: Catawba County Museum of History
rows.Notes: The museum hosted an exhibit (pictured) titled A Race To Remember: Catawba County's Soap Box Derby (1967–1972) , which opened on March 9, 2024.  It featured six Derby cars of local champions from those dates.  A film by Richard Eller, which features interviews of Hickory Derby director John Vaughn, as well as past racers,  was shown on the opening day, along with sales of a book titled Down the Hill – A Race to Remember that Eller compiled directly from transcripts of those interviews.

rows.Name: Catawba County Museum of History
rows.Notes: The exhibit included cars piloted by the following Champs: Mark Steven Cockerham winning in 1968, Mike Bolch in 1969, Keith Whitener in 1970, Keith Throneburg (pictured) in 1971, and Buster Carpenter in 1972. Rounding out the six was Andy Killian, who took 2nd in 1972. The exhibit ran through the summer.

rows.Name: Catawba County Museum of History
rows.Notes: Mike Bolch's 1969 car (pictured) has already been on display at the museum as early as 2018.

rows.Name: Clark County Historical Society
rows.Notes: Has in its collection a black Derby racer  (illustration pictured) piloted by 1951 Springfield, Ohio Champion Lawrence Nicholl, 12. The car is on exhibit at the Clark County Heritage Center in Springfield.

rows.Name: Clark County Museum
rows.Notes: On loan from the Nevada State Museum (see below) is a Derby racer piloted by Richard Paul Williams, who won the Las Vegas, Nevada Championship in 1958. The exhibit includes Richard’s car, a local trophy, helmet and jacket.

rows.Name: Clarksburg History Museum
rows.Notes: One of the new exhibits at the Clarksburg museum that was put on display in 2024 featured Soap Box Derby racers, including a red car from the 1950s.

rows.Name: Clinton County Historical Museum at Paine-Gillam-Scott House
rows.Notes: Received a Derby car (illustration pictured) donated by Kris Patterson,  winner of the St. Johns Championship in 1968.

rows.Name: Codington County Heritage Museum
rows.Notes: Has at least two cars, including one piloted by 1968 Watertown Champion Randall Kent Brandriet.

rows.Name: Cole Land Transportation Museum
rows.Notes: Has three Derby cars suspended high above the exhibit floor,   including those piloted by 1950 local champion James Roy (his car pictured), and 1957 champ Robert S. Briggs.

rows.Name: Colorado Springs Pioneers Museum
rows.Notes: Has an interactive exhibit titled Story of Us: Explore the History and Geography of the Pikes Peak Region ,  which features a Derby car piloted by 1947 local entry Al Bates.

rows.Name: Connecticut Science Center
rows.Notes: Has a racer piloted by 1999 World Rally Super Stock Champion Carleigh LeBlanc as part of the center's Sights & Sounds exhibit.

rows.Name: Corinth Maine Historical Society
rows.Notes: Is hosting an exhibit that features two racers from Corinth that competed in the 1948 Bangor , Maine local Derby race, piloted by Delwin and Gareth Blackwell.

rows.Name: Crawford Auto-Aviation Museum
rows.Notes: Has three racers,  including two on exhibit in a show titled Off the Rack: Hidden Treasures From the Crawford. They include a car piloted by 1946 Cleveland, Ohio Champion Richard Zoller, who took runner-up at the 9th All-American World Championship,  and a blue lay-down car (illustration pictured) piloted by Margaret Mary "Peggy" Zoller, who won the Cleveland Championship in 1973  and placed 6th at the All-American.  The exhibit is on until April 2026.

rows.Name: Darlington County Historical Commission
rows.Notes: The Darlington County Museum, which opened in 2018 as the Commission's exhibition venue, has two Derby cars on display.   They comprise a racer piloted by 1951 local Champion Tommy Jordan, who donated it in 2018,  and a laydown entry from the 1970s on loan from its driver Allan King,  who hailed from nearby Hartsville, South Carolina .

rows.Name: Deer Park Winery and Auto Museum
rows.Notes: Has three unidentified Derby cars from different decades on display side-by-side on an incline ramp situated above the exhibit floor.

rows.Name: DFW Car and Toy Museum
rows.Notes: A collection of Derby trophies and memorabilia was donated to the museum, including a racer  piloted by 1950 Springfield, OH Champion David F. Corbin,   and put on display.

rows.Name: Deming Luna Mimbers Museum
rows.Notes: Has two unidentified Derby cars from different decades on display,   including a Jack Kennedy Ford-sponsored, class A entry from the 1960s.

rows.Name: Depew House
rows.Notes: On June 9, 2024 the Orangetown Historical Museum & Archives hosted a talk titled Away We Go!  at Depew House, the exhibition venue used by the Museum.  The talk, celebrating the history of the Soap Box Derby in that region, was accompanied by Derby-related artifacts,  including a blue 1960s Derby car on display.

rows.Name: Detroit News Building
rows.Notes: Home of the Detroit News newspaper from 1917 to 2014, housed in its reference center a Derby car (illustration pictured) piloted by 1964 Suburban Detroit Champion Patrick Shorkey. By October 2014 it was one of the last remnants remaining  at the property while the newspaper was relocating to a new facility.

rows.Name: DieWerkhalle
rows.Notes: Opel , a major sponsor of the German Soap Box Derby from 1950 to 1971, hosted a pop-up event at DieWerkhalle,  an exhibition venue, that celebrated the 186th birthday of Opel founder Adam Opel . Under the motto Opel—Tradition Meets Future, the exhibit featured numerous artifacts from Opel's 150-year history, including a restored Derby racer piloted by 1957 local Champion Heinrich Walter.

rows.Name: Don Garlits Museum of Drag Racing
rows.Notes: Visible from the I-75 in Ocala, Florida, the Museum is a drag racing and motorsports-dedicated facility of vintage cars. It includes three Derby cars  (pictured) from the 1990s, comprising two Stock Division entries   and one Masters Division entry  piloted by 1996 Central Florida Masters Champion Ashlee Gravett.  Gravett is the granddaughter of 1933 Dayton, Ohio soap box entrant and 2000 All-American Soap Box Derby Hall of Fame inductee Robert Gravett,  who's Old #7 car was used on Derby's official logo from 1934 until the late 60s.

rows.Name: Don Laughlin's Classic Car Museum
rows.Notes: Has in its collection of vintage automobiles  a Derby car piloted by 1971 Las Vegas, NV Champion Terry Steve Leisek.

rows.Name: Douglas F. Cooley Memorial Art Gallery
rows.Notes: Hosted an exhibit by Brooklyn-based artist, activist and professor Gregg Bordowitz , titled I Wanna Be Well , an art installation on the AIDs pandemic continuing to exist worldwide. The exhibit included a piece titled Drive 2, which was a lay-down Derby car of unknown origin covered in vinyl stickers.  After the 2018 exhibit, it opened again in 2021 at MoMA PS1, a contemporary art institution located in New York (Queens), with the same Derby car.

rows.Name: DuBois Area Historical Society
rows.Notes: Hosted in concert with The Courier Express is a series of exhibits titled Turn Back the Clock , which in April 2024 featured a Derby car (illustration pictured) piloted by 1950 DuBois Champion James M. Shaffer, on display at the E. D. Reitz Museum in DuBois.

rows.Name: Duisburg Museum of Cultural and Urban History
rows.Notes: Hosted an exhibit titled 3, 2, 1 ... Start! about the history of the Soap Box Derby in that region from 1952 to 1971. Opening June 2013 and running until January 2014, the exhibit included artifacts, tours and talks by various speakers that raced and/or participated.

rows.Name: Eastern Museum of Motor Racing (EMMR)
rows.Notes: Has multiple Derby cars on exhibit,   including examples piloted by 1940 Harrisburg, Pennsylvania Champion Jack Finney,   1970 York County, Pennsylvania Champion Mark E. Ilgenfritz (illustration of car pictured),  and 1980 York, Pennsylvania Champion Chris Thorn.

rows.Name: Edge Motor Museum
rows.Notes: Has a Derby exhibit that features a car built and donated by Leslie Dale,   who was the class B champ in Nashville, Tennessee in 1940.

rows.Name: Eisenhower Conference Center
rows.Notes: Hosted an auction of historic wax figures on May 13, 2017, which included a Derby car  piloted by 1980 Montgomery, Alabama Senior Champion Allen Young.

rows.Name: Elkhorn Valley Museum
rows.Notes: Has a red Derby car from the mid- to late-seventies.

rows.Name: Ellwood City Area Historical Society
rows.Notes: Has on permanent display a Derby car (illustration pictured) piloted by 1959 Ellwood Champion Eddie Berendt.  Exhibited in 2019 was the Bernard "Bucky" Kline miniature collection of Ellwood Champions from 1936 to 1962, of which Berendt's car is replicated.

rows.Name: End of the Commons General Store
rows.Notes: Has on permanent display two Derby cars, including one (illustration pictured) piloted by 1960 Warren, OH Champion Allen Frantz, who donated it in 2015.

rows.Name: End of the Commons General Store
rows.Notes: 1961 Warren, OH entry James Chadwick (pictured), located above the retail floor alongside other memorabilia

rows.Name: Florence County Museum
rows.Notes: Hosted an exhibit highlighting the history of the annual Soap Box Derby race that took place in Florence during the 1960s and 1970s.

rows.Name: Floyd County Historical Museum
rows.Notes: Has a local entry  (illustration pictured) piloted in by Rick Justus, who won the Mason City, Iowa class B title in 1960.

rows.Name: Frankenmuth Historical Association
rows.Notes: Has a racer from 1968 Saginaw, Michigan Champ Marcus Haubenstricker.  The car is not on public display.

rows.Name: Fredericksburg Area Museum & Cultural Center
rows.Notes: Hosted an exhibit from June 16 to August 31, 2012, titled Thrill on the Hill ,  featuring a car (illustration pictured) piloted by 1959 Fredericksburg Champion Boyd E. Blevins. As of 2021 the car continues to be on exhibit.

rows.Name: Fredericksburg Area Museum & Cultural Center
rows.Notes: In 2025 a Soap Box Derby exhibit went on display featuring a Farmers Creamery-sponsored car (illustration pictured) piloted by William R. "Billy" Campbell,   a class A entrant in the Free Lance-Star Fredericksburg local race in 1961.

rows.Name: Gardner Museum
rows.Notes: Has a single racer piloted in 1938 by All-American third-placer Stanford Hartshorn.

rows.Name: Geary County Historical Society
rows.Notes: Has a single racer piloted in 1963 by Junction City, Kansas Champion Dana Wolf that was exhibited in 2013  and is now kept in their archive.

rows.Name: Gilmore Car Museum
rows.Notes: Has three Derby cars from the region exhibited on the showroom floor, each from a different decade,   and another suspended from the ceiling piloted by 1962 Kalamazoo , Michigan Champion Alan Richard Dean.

rows.Name: Giuseppe's Steel City Pizza
rows.Notes: Has among its extensive memorabilia décor a red, Pepsi Cola-sponsored Derby car from the 1960s hung on the wall.

rows.Name: Governor Motor Company
rows.Notes: Has a single racer (pictured) piloted by 1970 Southwest Suburban, Illinois Champion Mark T. Ahlgrim.

rows.Name: Greater Southwest Historical Museum
rows.Notes: Has two examples on display, including a 1970/71 racer piloted by Alan Sharp.

rows.Name: Greensboro History Museum
rows.Notes: Is hosting an exhibit titled GHM100: Treasures. Legacies. Remix  that includes a Derby racer  (illustration pictured) from the Museum's collection  piloted by 1959 Greensboro Champion Joe Harmon.  The exhibit lasts until Spring 2027.

rows.Name: Greenwood Antiques
rows.Notes: Has an unrestored car (illustration pictured) piloted by 1965 Charlottesville, Virginia Champion Donald Reid Jr. on the front veranda of the store.

rows.Name: Hartley Nature Center
rows.Notes: Once the site of Duluth's Soap Box Derby track, the center has a car (illustration pictured) piloted by 1964 Duluth Champion Dale Mell   to honor that legacy.

rows.Name: Hattiesburg Area Historical Society
rows.Notes: Has a racer  piloted in 1971 by Hattiesburg, Mississippi entrant Steve Mozingo.

rows.Name: Heinz History Center
rows.Notes: Hosted an exhibit from March 22 to October 6, 2024 titled A Woman’s Place: How Women Shaped Pittsburgh , which included a Soap Box Derby display that featured a car piloted by 1982 Western Pennsylvania Senior Champion Jessica Clark.

rows.Name: Hennepin History Museum
rows.Notes: Has a racer piloted by 1959 Minneapolis Champion Jerald Edward Houk.

rows.Name: The Henry Ford Museum
rows.Notes: Showcases 1939 North Platte, NE Champion Mason Colbert's racer   (illustration pictured).

rows.Name: Hessenpark
rows.Notes: Is hosting at Stallscheune aus Asterode, an exbibition venue in Hessenpark, a show titled Toys. Is It All Just a Game?  that features numerous children's toys from 1900 to the present day. Among the artifacts are German Soap Box Derby items,  including a restored Derby car from the 1950s.

rows.Name: High Point Museum
rows.Notes: Hosted from February to March 2023 a Derby-themed exhibit featuring photographs of past participants, memorabilia and a single racer (pictured) driven by 1953 High Point, North Carolina racer Henry Clyde Williams Jr. (1937–2022).  A panel discussion and question period was also held on the last Saturday of the exhibit. Invited to speak were Harrison "Bud" Lyon of Durham, the first African-American youth to win High Point's Derby in 1954; Bill Blair Jr., who participated in High Point's first Soap Box Derby in 1951;  and Gail Simpson, one of the first girls to race and the first to win High Point's Derby in 1972.  Ms. Simpson was unable to speak due to an illness.

rows.Name: Historical Auto Attractions
rows.Notes: Has a red sit-up Derby racer piloted by Bob Schmidt, who competed in 1954 and 1955 in Springfield, Illinois . Along with the car are Derby artifacts like helmets, a trophy and Official Derby literature.

rows.Name: Historical and Genealogical Society of Indiana County
rows.Notes: Has in its collection a Derby car donated in 2002 by owner and 1957 Indiana, Pennsylvania Champion Kennard Fairman.   The car was exhibited in 2022,  along with trophies for his Championship win in Indiana and his Best-Design award at the 20th All-American World Championship in Akron later that summer.

rows.Name: Historical Society of the Cocalico Valley
rows.Notes: Has on exhibit a racer  piloted by Mike Ocker, who took the class B runner-up and 4th overall in Reading, Pennsylvania in 1969.

rows.Name: The History Center in Tompkins County
rows.Notes: Had on exhibit a racer piloted by 1970 Ithaca, New York entry Robert Neigh.

rows.Name: Hitzacker Museum
rows.Notes: Is hosting a Derby exhibit of two cars that raced in the region, including an early–seventies laydown entry piloted by Björn Briese.   Accompanying the cars are documents and photos, as well as a 1950s film-viewing in November,  encompassing the history of the sport in Hitzacker.

rows.Name: Hi-Way Diner Lincoln
rows.Notes: Has on display a Derby car (illustration pictured) piloted by 1972 Claremont, New Hampshire Champion Mike Wise. The car is suspended upside-down from the ceiling.

rows.Name: Ice House Museum
rows.Notes: The Cedar Falls Historical Society exhibits artifacts from its collection at the Ice House Museum, a former ice house servicing the City of Cedar Falls. Part of that collection are three Derby cars from the region, a black racer piloted by 1954 Cedar Falls Champion John Thode,  a blue 1977/78 Junior Division entry by Terri Jerke,  and a yellow 1978/79 Junior entry by Terri's younger brother Mike.  As recent as 2018 they were also on exhibit.

rows.Name: Indianapolis Motor Speedway Museum
rows.Notes: Accepted a car (illustration pictured) piloted by 1954 Hartford, Connecticut Soap Box Derby Champion Denny Zimmerman ,  who donated it in 2007.

rows.Name: Indiana State Museum
rows.Notes: Has on exhibit in its Global Indiana gallery a Derby car  piloted by 1971 Lawrenceburg, Indiana Champion Kendall Jay Meyer.

rows.Name: International Motorsports Hall of Fame
rows.Notes: Has two Derby cars on exhibit, a 1960s entry from Birmingham, Alabama piloted by Matt Wright,   and a second by two-time (1997 and 1998) Birmingham, Alabama National Derby Rally (NDR) Masters Champion Will Waldrip.

rows.Name: Isett Heritage Museum
rows.Notes: Has three Derby racers from different generations on exhibit,   including a car piloted by 1958 Ellwood City, Pennsylvania entry Chuck Maggi, a kit-car by 1987 State College, Pennsylvania Junior Division Champion Karen Maggi and a laydown by 1990 Central Pennsylvania Masters Division Champion  Pamela Maggi.

rows.Name: James Madison Museum
rows.Notes: Has a single Derby car piloted by Johnny Altman, who raced in Orange and won the Best Constructed Award in 1960. Mr. Altman donated the car in 2013.

rows.Name: Jeff Matthews Memorial Museum
rows.Notes: This historical artifact museum celebrating Galax's pre- and post-colonial heritage has on exhibit a locally sponsored Derby racer accompanied by an official 1952 Derby helmet sitting atop the car.

rows.Name: Johnson County Museum
rows.Notes: Has a racer  piloted by 1967 Kansas City, Missouri Champion Dennis Mullen.

rows.Name: Kalamazoo Valley Museum
rows.Notes: Has a racer   (illustration pictured) piloted by Edward L. Cherkoian, 14, who won the Kalamazoo, Michigan local Championship in 1959  and competed at the 22nd All-American Nationals in Akron, Ohio a month later.  It is exhibited in the Atrium of Artifacts on the top level.

rows.Name: Kansas Historical Society
rows.Notes: Has a racer in its collection that was piloted but Russell Dille,  who took sixth place in the local Topeka Derby race in 1973.  Included with the car is related memorabilia like Dille's helmet and photos of him constructing the car. As recent a 2022 the car was on exhibit at the Kansas Museum of History in Topeka.

rows.Name: Kassel Museum
rows.Notes: Hosted an exhibit entitled "Es Lebe der Sport",  which featured a racer (illustration pictured) piloted by 1957 Kassel, Germany Soap Box Derby Champion Ernst Krönert.

rows.Name: Kingsport Archives
rows.Notes: Located on the 5th floor of the Kingsport City Hall building, the Kingsport Archives celebrated its 30th anniversary by hosting an open house on 3 October 2024 titled 30 Days of 30 Facts.  On display from its collection was a Derby racer piloted by 1970 Kingsport Champion Wayne D. Eldreth.   Also in its collection is a racer  piloted by 1965 Kingsport, TN class A entrant George Collins that he donated in 2004.

rows.Name: Kosciusko County Historical Society
rows.Notes: Exhibited at their 49th annual banquet was a Derby racer piloted in 1955 and 1956 by Larry Shively. Held at the Zimmer Biomet Center Lake Pavilion in Warsaw, speakers also included fellow racer Tom Plew, who came second at the local championship in 1957.

rows.Name: Kossuth County Agricultural and Motorsports Museum
rows.Notes: Has three Derby cars  on the second level of the museum. They include a metal sit-up racer piloted by Darrell Ludwig,  who took the Best-Constructed Car Award in the Algona, Iowa local race in 1950.  Alongside is a car (illustration pictured) piloted by Jackie Lichter (1933—2025),   who won the 1946 class B division in Algona and class B runner-up at the Iowa State Championship in Des Moines .  A publicity stunt prior to that race saw Bob Hope sitting astride his car.  Lichter raced again in 1947, winning the class A division trophy in Algona.  His car in the museum is restored to 1947 livery. A third car in the museum is unidentified.

rows.Name: Lancaster Soap Box Derby Hall of Fame Museum
rows.Notes: Has a large collection (pictured) of their local champ cars on display at their topside building.  Some of their earliest entries, all sit-ups, include those piloted by Scott Straley in 1956—their oldest car, Jerry Campbell in 1957, Don McCellan in 1958, Dick Kraner in 1959, Larry Wilkins in 1960, Larry McCoy in 1961, Ben McCoy in 1963, Jeff Engel in 1964, David Beach in 1966  (illustration pictured below), Rick Wilkins in 1967, Jim Hunt in 1969 and David Brenstuhl in 1970. Early lay-down models include Ray Blair in 1971, Pike Hull in 1972, Bill Hunt in 1973, Brian Hunt in 1974 (pictured below), Mike Roth in 1975, Ken Hoffman in 1976, Lisa Spires in 1977 and Lori Roth in 1978.

rows.Name: Lancaster Soap Box Derby Hall of Fame Museum
rows.Notes: 1966 Lancaster, Ohio Champion David Beach's car (illustration pictured)

rows.Name: Lancaster Soap Box Derby Hall of Fame Museum
rows.Notes: 1974 Lancaster, Ohio Champion Brian Hunt's car (pictured) on exhibit at the 2nd Annual Vintage Derby Car Show in 2023

rows.Name: Lauderdale County Archives
rows.Notes: The Lauderdale County Department of Archives & History Inc. acquired in 2025 a Derby car that was donated by its original owner, 1963 Meridian, Mississippi Champion W. L. Landrum.

rows.Name: Larz Anderson Auto Museum
rows.Notes: Has suspended from the wall a black Derby racer piloted in 1949 by Ronald Meletzke from Cleveland, Ohio, and a 1953 helmet hung alongside.

rows.Name: The LeMay – America's Car Museum
rows.Notes: Has two examples, including a car piloted by 1967 Tacoma, Washington Champion Richard R. Peterson,   and 1972 Seattle, Washington Champion Mark Spencer Chamberlain.

rows.Name: Lorain County History Center
rows.Notes: Has a Derby racer in pristine condition that was piloted in 1967 by Amherst, Ohio Champion David W. Gard (1953–2006).  Gard's children donated the car and its memorabilia in 2012,  which has remained on exhibit by the main entrance ever since.

rows.Name: Lynchburg Museum
rows.Notes: Exhibited three Derby cars in 2012 that competed in Lynchburg's local race.  One of them on permanent display    was piloted by Terrell Griffin, who competed from 1949 until 1951.

rows.Name: Lynchburg Police Department HQ Museum
rows.Notes: The Lynchburg Police Foundation acquired for its future memorabilia museum a Derby racer (illustration pictured) donated by Claude and Martha Tuggle. Claude raced the car in 1951 when he was 14-years old. His sponsor was the LPD, where his father served as police sergeant on the force.

rows.Name: The Magnolia Plantation Bed & Breakfast Inn
rows.Notes: Has a Derby car on the verandah of the inn,  photographed and posted in a review dated September 2016.  The red sit-up car, named "Spats" Hurricane , was raced by 1966 Ft. Pierce, Florida entrant Joey Montalto.

rows.Name: Mattatuck Museum
rows.Notes: Hosted from January 2023 to January 2024 a Derby-themed installation featuring pamphlets, photographs  and a 1971 racer loaned by its owner, driver Stephen Longo.

rows.Name: McHenry County Historical Society & Museum
rows.Notes: Has a car piloted by 1952 Woodstock, Illinois Champion Peter Perkins,  who is a life member of the museum.

rows.Name: Memory Lane Museum
rows.Notes: Has twenty-one vintage Derby cars (pictured) in their collection.  They include examples from Dan Parks of Charlotte, North Carolina, who finished his long career in 1965 as a class A;  Neil Castles Jr., also of Charlotte, who took 6th place in the Senior Division of that local in 1985;  and Mark Whitley of Winston-Salem, North Carolina, who competed at the All-American in 1990 in the Kit Division, winning his first heat.  The following year he raced as a Senior at the All-American, taking 8th.

rows.Name: Memory Lane Museum
rows.Notes: A white sit-up racer (pictured) piloted by Steve Matlock of Knoxville, TN, who competed from 1955 to 1958, taking 2nd in 1956

rows.Name: Memory Lane Museum
rows.Notes: A blue sit-up racer (pictured) piloted by Carson, Virginia entrant Freddie Shultz

rows.Name: Miller House Museum
rows.Notes: Curated by the Washington County Historical Society, which is headquartered at the Miller House Museum, is an exbibit of a restored Derby car (illustration pictured) piloted in 1939 by Hagerstown, Maryland Champion Lewis Spessard (1923–2018).  The car was restored a month prior to its unveiling on March 1, 2025.

rows.Name: Minnesota History Center
rows.Notes: Has a Derby car piloted in 1938  by St. Paul, Minnesota Champion Herbert Garelic.

rows.Name: Miracle of America Museum
rows.Notes: Has a Derby car (illustration pictured) in its collection that was piloted by 1946 Bay City, Michigan Champion Douglas Swisher.  Racing in Flint, Michigan, Swisher was a class A competitor against other Bay City entrants for that community's top prize.

rows.Name: Miriam P. Brenner Children's Museum
rows.Notes: Has three Derby cars from the 1970s suspended above the Volvo truck and Petty Enterprises Hot Wheels exhibits.   They were all constructed and raced by Greensboro, North Carolina competitor Eddie Ross,  who was runner-up finalist in 1973.

rows.Name: Mission Museum
rows.Notes: Has at least four Derby cars that competed locally, including a yellow entry (illustration pictured) piloted by 1961 Mission City, British Columbia Champion Raymond Mack.

rows.Name: Mission Museum
rows.Notes: A second example (pictured) piloted by 1969 Western Canada Champion Dennis Lissimore

rows.Name: Monroe County History Center
rows.Notes: Has on exbibit two examples, including a blue car from the 1950s piloted by an unidentified driver,   and a second by Bloomington, Indiana entrant Gerry Patterson, who was runner-up in 1962.

rows.Name: Morrison Motor Car Museum
rows.Notes: Has two cars (pictured) piloted by 1965 Charlotte, North Carolina Champion David Alexander, and 1966 Charlotte, North Carolina racer Mark Alexander on the showroom floor.

rows.Name: Muscatine Art Center
rows.Notes: Is hosting an exhibit titled Muscatine History Revisited from October 2024 to August 2025 that features a Derby car named The Melon Shed  piloted in 1949 by Muscatine class B Champion Jim Hoopes.

rows.Name: Museu da Casa Brasileira
rows.Notes: Held an exhibit titled Design Aerodinâmico – Metáfora do Futuro  (en. Aerodynamic Design – Metaphor for the Future ), featuring a 1940s Derby car from Portsmouth, New Hampshire .

rows.Name: Museum der Niederrheinischen Seele
rows.Notes: Housed at the Villa Erckens, the Museum added to their collection a yellow sit-up racer piloted by Georg Briese, who in 1985 competed at the first Derby race in Grevenbroich and in 2021 donated the car.

rows.Name: Museum Im Stern
rows.Notes: Following the 75th anniversary of Warburg October Week,  a series of personal mementos connected to the festivities were put on display from late-October to mid-November 2024, including at the Museum a Derby car piloted by 1968 Warburg Champion Klaus Braun.

rows.Name: Museum of American Speed
rows.Notes: Has numerous Derby cars on exhibit,  including examples piloted by 1934 Indianapolis, Indiana Champion Raymond A. Kern, 1949–51 Muncie, Indiana class B racer Garland Ross Jr. (illustration pictured), 1962 Detroit, MI Champion Robert Joseph Hanlon, as well as 1969 entries from Mark Larivee of Detroit and local Steve Fralin of Lincoln.

rows.Name: Museum of American Speed
rows.Notes: Also on exhibit is a soap box racer (illustration pictured) piloted by Henry Yacek, who competed in the inaugural Naugatuck, Connecticut Coasting Derby , an un-registered Soap Box Derby event in 1948, receiving a plaque for best designed car.  It was donated by Henry and Irene Yacek.

rows.Name: National Automotive and Truck Museum
rows.Notes: Home of GM Futurliner#10 ,  has on display numerous Derby cars from various decades and race divisions,   including a blue class B entry from the 1960s,  and an orange lay-down design from the 1970s.

rows.Name: National Museum of American History
rows.Notes: Has several Derby items, including two racers and a helmet. One racer (illustration pictured) was piloted by 1961 Hartford, Connecticut Champion Robert J. Pusateri,  and the second by 1994 National Derby Rally Stock Division Champion Laura Shepherd   from Kent, Ohio . The cars are not on public display. The helmet in the collection  was worn by Derby's first female World Champion Karren Stead, who won in 1975.

rows.Name: Nevada State Museum
rows.Notes: The Nevada State Museum conducted an exhibit hosted at the Las Vegas Springs Preserve titled Eclectic Nevada, which included a Derby car piloted by 1958 Las Vegas, Nevada Champion Richard Paul Williams.

rows.Name: New England Racing Museum
rows.Notes: Has three Derby cars hung on a wall display,    including one piloted by 1982 Junior World Champion Carol Ann Sullivan. 1954 Hartford, Connecticut Champion Denny Zimmermans's car (illustration pictured) was on exhibit there in 2021,  on loan from the Indianapolis Motor Speedway Museum .

rows.Name: New York State Museum
rows.Notes: Hosted in 2010 an exhibition titled Derby Doings: The All-American Soap Box Derby , which celebrated the history of the sport and specifically Albany's participation in it, with its first competition held in 1940. Featured were two local Derby cars, one built by 1949 entry Richard Russell and a Super-Stock entry piloted by Michael Morawski, who raced in 2007.  In 2018 the museum acquired a car (illustration pictured) piloted by 1971 Albany, New York Champion Randy Hood, along with his race jacket and trophy.

rows.Name: North Carolina Museum of History
rows.Notes: Has a single racer (illustration pictured) in their collection, piloted by 1972 Chapel Hill, North Carolina Champion Priscilla Freeman, who took fifth place at the 35th All-American.  The car is currently not on public display.

rows.Name: Northwest Connecticut Fire Fighting Museum
rows.Notes: Situated at the Bad Dog Brewing Company in Torrington, has two Derby car as floor exhibits, both sponsored by the Torrington Fire Department,   including an example piloted by Tommy Petrovits.

rows.Name: Oakland Museum of California
rows.Notes: Hosted an exhibit by artist Mark Dion titled The Marvelous Museum , that featured overlooked "orphans, curiosities, and treasures" seldom displayed nor borrowed by other museums.  In it a Derby car (illustration pictured) from pre-1948  was included, and was like many of the items in the exhibit presented in its storage crate.  The car was gifted to the Museum by Bill Jolliffe, who is credited as its maker.

rows.Name: Ohio History Center
rows.Notes: Has a Derby car on display piloted by 1949 Akron, Ohio 3rd-placer Carl William "Bill" Ford.

rows.Name: Okoboji Classic Cars
rows.Notes: Has three Derby cars on display, including one (illustration pictured) from 1966 Sioux City, Iowa Champion Roger Lee Van Waart.

rows.Name: Old Courthouse Museum
rows.Notes: Has two cars in a Derby exhibit,   including 1970 Sioux Falls, South Dakota entry Evan Jones and 1971 Sioux Falls Champion Steve Peterson.

rows.Name: Old School Museum
rows.Notes: Has a Champion car from Clint Buckley who won the Jacksonville, Illinois , local race in 1972.

rows.Name: Old State House Museum
rows.Notes: Has a racer (illustration pictured) piloted by 1960 Magnolia, Arkansas Champion Wallace F. Waits (1945–2023).   The car is currently not on public display.

rows.Name: Olean Historical Society
rows.Notes: Has two sit-up Derby racers on exhibit that were piloted by brothers Dick and Gary Montgomery in the late 1950s.

rows.Name: Osoyoos & District Museum and Archives
rows.Notes: Has a small Soap Box Derby collection that includes an Official All-American racing jacket worn by 1960 Western Canada Champion Holger Huhn, a silver Derby racing helmet from 1962, and an unidentified green race car from the late-fifties or early-sixties.

rows.Name: Owls Head Transportation Museum
rows.Notes: The museum has a wealth of Derby-related ephemera in its archives and several cars tucked away in storage, including 1938 Portland, Maine Champion Perley Bartlett.  As recent as 2017, it along with two others were exhibited in the museum.

rows.Name: Parsons Historical Society Museum
rows.Notes: Hosted an exhibit of Derby memorabilia that featured at least four cars,  including examples piloted by 1949 local Champion William Schibi  and 1950 local Champion Jerry Schibi.

rows.Name: Peekskill Museum
rows.Notes: Has a single example (pictured) upstairs in the Marion Boyle Children's Room, piloted by 1936 Peekskill, New York Champion William Barthelmes.

rows.Name: Pennsylvania College of Technology
rows.Notes: Pennsylvania College of Technology, which opens its masonry laboratory annually for construction of cars used in the Williamsport Soap Box Derby, exhibited in 2012 a Derby car piloted by 1951 World Champion Darwin Cooper, who hails from there. The car was put on display at the entrance of the college's Madigan Library .

rows.Name: Region of Waterloo Museums & Archives
rows.Notes: Has in their collection a class B car (pictured) built in 1955 and raced in the area. The driver's name is withheld pending permission of the donor, who was original owner and builder of the car.  It is currently not on public display.

rows.Name: Richardson County Historical Society
rows.Notes: Had added their collection in 2023 two Derby cars from the late 1940s that were donated by their original owners. They were piloted by local racers Ward Reesman in 1948 and Ray Simon in 1949.

rows.Name: Rock County Historical Society
rows.Notes: Housed at Lincoln-Tallman House in Janesville, and in the basement, are two cars in a Derby-themed exhibit  piloted by 1948 Janesville, Wisconsin Champion Carliss H. Shuler (illustration pictured) and 1949 Janesville, Wisconsin Champion Gerald S. Wells.

rows.Name: Route 66 Motorheads Bar and Grill and Museum
rows.Notes: Situated above the restaurant bar is a Derby car  piloted by 1972 Springfield, Illinois Champion Robert Wayne Wieks, along with other memorabilia like a flag and trophy connected to the car's history. Mr. Wieks hadn't seen the car since his win in 1972 until much later when it was put on display above the bar. Now back in his possession, the car remains on exhibit.

rows.Name: Ruhr Museum
rows.Notes: Hosted an exhibit titled Childhood in the Ruhr Region , which included a Derby racer from Essen piloted by Hardy Hausberg in 1983.

rows.Name: St. Catharines Museum & Welland Canals Centre
rows.Notes: Hosted a Derby-themed exhibit on the history of the Soap Box Derby in St. Catharines featuring photographs, trophies and related memorabilia.  In it were two cars piloted by 1954 Champ Larry Tracey (illustration pictured), which is in the Museum's permanent collection,  and 1972 Champ William Roy "Bill" Hand.

rows.Name: St. Louis County Historical Society
rows.Notes: Hosted an exhibit at the Fesler Gallery on 1963 Soap Box Derby World Champion Harold "Bo" Conrad, who hailed from Duluth, Minnesota. On display was a blue Derby car and videos, with trophies and memorabilia on loan from Mr. Conrad.    The car he won in (illustration pictured) is on exhibit at the Soap Box Derby Hall of Fame Museum in Akron, Ohio

rows.Name: San Diego Automotive Museum
rows.Notes: Exhibited a Derby racer (illustration pictured) piloted by 1946 World Champion Gilbert Klecan, who loaned the car.

rows.Name: Sanford Museum & Planetarium
rows.Notes: Has hosted several Derby cars, including a Soap Box Derby exhibit  that ran until March 18, 2024.  They have included examples piloted by 1954 Sioux City, Iowa racer Martin Boothby,  and 1971 Cherokee, Iowa Champion Jim Krueger.

rows.Name: Saratoga Automobile Museum
rows.Notes: Has exhibited vintage racers piloted by Peter Voronovsky (illustration pictured) of Schenectady, New York ,   who was awarded the Best Constructed trophy in 1951,  and Jordan Milner of Windsor, Connecticut , who competed as a Stock Division entry in 1995.

rows.Name: Saratoga Automobile Museum
rows.Notes: Linda Lee Aidala was Albany, New York  Senior Division Champion in her orange lay-down racer (illustration pictured) in 1981.

rows.Name: Seiverling Museum
rows.Notes: Seiverling Museum, a car and pedal car museum, entered a float at the 88th Ephrata Fair Parade,  which featured a Derby car piloted by 1973 local Champion Brad Kreider, whose family members were volunteers. The parade took place on Main Street, the same thoroughfare on which Brad had won 50 years earlier.

rows.Name: Silver Creek Museum
rows.Notes: Has a single example piloted by 1950–1951 Freeport, Illinois racer Dean G. Speilman.

rows.Name: Simpson County Historical Society
rows.Notes: Featured a Soap Box Derby exhibit in their window display, including a car piloted by 1963 Bowling Green, Kentucky Champion Jim Clouse  and a second by Conleigh Wilson, who raced from 2014 until 2018 and then loaned the car to D.J. Kriser, who won the Franklin Junior Championship in 2019.

rows.Name: Sioux City Public Museum
rows.Notes: Has at least four cars, including a replica of 1937 Sioux City, Iowa Champion Wayne Johnson's "mushroom car", which he constructed in 2008 and donated to the museum,  and 1967 Sioux City, Iowa Champion Mark Lehmann  (1953–2017)  (illustration of his car pictured), both suspended high above the museum floor.

rows.Name: Sioux City Public Museum
rows.Notes: In 2023 a show entitled New to You: Recent Artifact Donations exhibited recent acquisitions, including two Derby cars driven by 1970 Sioux City, Iowa Champion Stephen T. Lalley  (illustration pictured) and 1990 Sioux City, Iowa Masters Champion Wendy Van Waart.

rows.Name: Sloan Museum of Discovery
rows.Notes: Exhibited in the Durant Vehicle Gallery of the Sloan Museum in Flint, Michigan is a collection of Derby memorabilia   commemorating Flint's involvement in the sport since 1938.  Prominent are two Derby cars, a black sit-up entry piloted by Flint Champion Steven A. Katz,   who made it to the second round of the 23rd All-American World Championship in 1960,  and a white laydown entry piloted by Flint Senior Division Champion Mark Smith,  who tied for runner-up at the 44th All-American in 1981.

rows.Name: Smoky Hill Museum
rows.Notes: Has exhibited  a Derby car piloted by 1967 Salina, Kansas Champion Jack Klein  (1955–2004).

rows.Name: Soap Box Derby Hall of Fame Museum
rows.Notes: Home of the Soap Box Derby , the Hall of Fame Museum houses about half of the 140+ vehicles that won the All-American World Championship.  They include a replica of Robert Gravett's Old #7 racer from 1933 used in the official logo,  and 1947 World Champion Kenneth Holmboe (illustration of his car pictured).

rows.Name: Soap Box Derby Hall of Fame Museum
rows.Notes: 1952 World Champion Joe Lunn's racer (illustration pictured), dubbed "The Ramblin' Wreck from Georgia"

rows.Name: Soap Box Derby Hall of Fame Museum
rows.Notes: 1961 Colorado Springs, Colorado entrant Bob Carter's racer (pictured) was donated in 2012.

rows.Name: Soap Box Derby Hall of Fame Museum
rows.Notes: 1963 World Champion Harold Conrad's racer (illustration pictured)

rows.Name: Soap Box Derby Hall of Fame Museum
rows.Notes: Ken Cline's 1967 World Championship racer (illustration pictured), dubbed "the Grasshopper"

rows.Name: Soap Box Derby Hall of Fame Museum
rows.Notes: Soap Box Derby's first female All-American Champion Karren Stead has her car  (illustration pictured) on exhibit at the Museum. The helmet she used is in the collection of the National Museum of American History .

rows.Name: Soap Box Derby Hall of Fame Museum
rows.Notes: 1983 Senior World Champion Mike Burdgick's lay-down racer (illustration pictured)

rows.Name: Soap Box Derby Hall of Fame Museum
rows.Notes: 1992 Masters World Champion Bonnie Thornton's sit-up racer (illustration pictured)

rows.Name: South Dakota State Historical Society
rows.Notes: Has a Derby car (illustration pictured) in its collection that was piloted by 1941 Rapid City, South Dakota Champion Jack Enterman.

rows.Name: Stables Cafe
rows.Notes: Has as part its extensive antiques collection an unidentified lay-down racer from the 1970s suspended above the dining area.

rows.Name: Stansbury Museum
rows.Notes: Located on Gulf St Vincent across from Adelaide , South Australia, this local museum has a yellow 1970s, layback Derby car named Rusty's Racer on display.

rows.Name: Stratford-Perth Archives
rows.Notes: Displayed a derby car (illustration pictured) in 2019 dubbed "Miss Canada," which was raced in Stratford from 1951 to 1954 by brothers Gary and Marvin Thomas. The car is in the collection of the Stratford Perth Museum, who loaned the car.

rows.Name: Strong National Museum of Play
rows.Notes: Has multiple examples in their collection, including cars piloted by 1951 Rochester, New York class A racer Richard E. "Dick" Zicari  (1936–2011),  donated by Mr. Zicari (illustration pictured), 1964 Rochester Champion William Lentzer, which has been on display as recent as 2018,  and 1975 Rochester Champion Dave Marra, donated by Mr. Marra.

rows.Name: Subsequence Magazine
rows.Notes: Subsequence Magazine, self-described as "an experimental media project," curated in 2022 and 2023 a pop-up gallery titled Subsequence SALON vol.2 My Archive that displayed a variety of arts and crafts,  including an unidentified Derby car  of 1970s layback design and laminate construction.

rows.Name: Swift Current Museum
rows.Notes: Hosted a Derby exhibit in October 2018 that was pitched to the museum by the Swift Current Soapbox Racing Association, which at the time was celebrating 35 years of continuous racing. It featured several racers, including a senior lay-down car piloted by Aiden Jahnke.

rows.Name: Syracuse Sports Hall of Fame
rows.Notes: Has a single Derby car piloted by 1970 Syracuse Champion Walter G. Hadyk.

rows.Name: Tallahassee Automobile Museum
rows.Notes: Has three cars on exhibit, including examples from Roy Garren, who raced in the Senior Division in the DeKalb County, Georgia , race in 1984, and David Garren, who won the Junior Division Championship in Atlanta in 1985.

rows.Name: Tallmadge Historical Society
rows.Notes: Has a 1976 Junior (the inaugural year for the Junior Division) racer (illustration pictured) that was piloted by Suzanne Miller, who won the Flint, MI Fall Rally Jr. Championship that year. Suzanne hailed from Tallmadge, Ohio, where the first Soap Box Derby race was held, down Tallmadge Hill, in Akron, Ohio in 1934.

rows.Name: Toronto Motorama
rows.Notes: A single example, an all metal-clad racer from the 1960s, was exhibited in the Bodymotive Services kiosk at the Motorama Custom Car & Motorsports Expo in 2020.  In 2022 the car competed at the Elora, Ontario soapbox derby.

rows.Name: Trans-Allegheny Lunatic Asylum
rows.Notes: Has a single racer   piloted by Cumberland, Maryland entry Donald Saville of Romney, West Virginia ,  who competed as a class B entry in 1954, winning two heats, and a class A the following year.

rows.Name: T.T. Wentworth Museum
rows.Notes: Now the Pensacola Museum of History , the former T.T. Wentworth Museum hosted in 2017 an exhibit titled From the Vault: Why and What We Collect , showcasing 120 artifacts described as "strange, beautiful and fascinating, from the University of West Florida Historic Trust collection."  Among the artifacts was a Derby car  piloted by 1961 Pensacola, Florida Champion Pat Ratley.

rows.Name: Tustin Area Historical Museum
rows.Notes: Exhibited on June 11, 2021, a racer (illustration pictured) piloted by 1948 Sidney, Nebraska Champion Marlin Clark, with Mr. Clark speaking of his Derby experience to guests in attendance.

rows.Name: Tyler History Center
rows.Notes: Has two cars on display, piloted by 1967 class A entry James Strock  and 1968 racer Donald Del Cessna,  both who competed in Youngstown.

rows.Name: Unser Racing Museum
rows.Notes: Featured two Derby cars  piloted by 1960 Albuquerque, New Mexico Champion Lawrence Martin  and 1966 Albuquerque, New Mexico Champion Richard E. Martin.  The museum closed in 2023, with its collection being relocated to the Museum of American Speed in Lincoln, Nebraska.

rows.Name: Vance-Tousey House
rows.Notes: Hosted an exhibit titled The Great Race ,  featuring a Derby racer piloted by 1969 Lawrenceburg, Indiana Champion Alfred Dewayne Uhlman.

rows.Name: Verdigris Tea & Chocolate
rows.Notes: Hosted a fine art exhibit of paintings by Jack Fenn in the Verdigris Gallery from February 26 to April 1, 2025.  Mr. Fenn participated in the Soap Box Derby in 1956 in Greenport, New York and exhibited his extant car (illustration pictured) alongside his work.

rows.Name: Vintage Derby Car Show
rows.Notes: Annual exhibit taking place during Race Week that culminates in the All-American World Championship in Akron, Ohio. The exhibit showcases extant vintage Derby racers and memorabilia that invites any and all Derby alumni to attend and participate, and is open to the general public. At its inaugural exhibit in 2022 an array of classic Derby car designs (pictured) was put on display.

rows.Name: Vintage Derby Car Show
rows.Notes: Oldest car (pictured) piloted by at the 3rd Vintage Show in 2024 piloted by 1952 Soap Box Derby World Champion Joe Lunn, showing collision damage

rows.Name: Vintage Derby Car Show
rows.Notes: Oldest car (pictured) at the 2nd Vintage Show in 2023 piloted by Indianapolis, Indiana Champion David M. Knight in 1953

rows.Name: Vintage Derby Car Show
rows.Notes: 1956 Valparaiso, Indiana entrant Doug Hoback's car (pictured) at the 3rd Vintage Show in 2024

rows.Name: Vintage Derby Car Show
rows.Notes: An original and unrestored racer (pictured) piloted by 1961 Ashland, Ohio Champion James Stine

rows.Name: Vintage Derby Car Show
rows.Notes: A sit-up racer (pictured) piloted by 1961 Mansfield, Ohio Champion Timothy Boyer at the 3rd Vintage Show in 2024

rows.Name: Vintage Derby Car Show
rows.Notes: 1969 New Philadelphia, Ohio Champion Jeff Bitticker's car (pictured) at the 3rd Vintage Show in 2024

rows.Name: Vintage Derby Car Show
rows.Notes: A blue laydown car (illustration pictured) 1974 Conshohocken, Pennsylvania Champion Edward L. Myers (1961–2025), who took 3rd at the 37th All-American and set the current track speed record in Akron.

rows.Name: Virginia Museum of Transportation
rows.Notes: Has on exhibit a tree-display of four Derby cars (pictured) from different decades. They include, from the top, Tim Royer's orange Super Stock car from 2001 to 2003,  Roanoke, Virginia Champion Michael Jay Dobie's blue car from 1966,  Roanoke, Virginia Champion Charles "Kim" Lineberry III's yellow car from 1969,  and an unidentified red entry from the 1950s. As recent as March 2025 Dobie's blue car was not part of the display.

rows.Name: Vortaunus Museum
rows.Notes: Has numerous cars on exhibit, including those piloted by 1950 German Champion Alfred Hänle, 1955 German Champion Heinz Soethof, 1967 German Champion Klaus Rohde, 1968 German Champion Bernd Schacherl, 1971 German Champion Karl-Heinz Peter  and 1983  German Sr. Champion Rieke Monschauer.

rows.Name: Waukesha County Historical Society & Museum
rows.Notes: Exhibited a car (illustration pictured) piloted by 1947 Waukesha, Wisconsin Champion Jack Chapman (1932–2019).

rows.Name: Wayne County Historical Museum
rows.Notes: Has several cars suspended above the museum floor,  including one piloted by 1968 Richmond, Indiana Champion James B. Wells II.

rows.Name: Westerwald Landscape Museum
rows.Notes: Hosted an exhibit titled Das Zeitalter des Kleinwagenwunders which celebrated the post-War emergence of small and micro-sized automobiles.  In it was a display of German Soap Box Derby memorabilia and a single 1950s or 1960s car from that region.

rows.Name: Whataburger
rows.Notes: Located at 5003 Troup Highway in Tyler, TX, this fast food restaurant has an interior décor that honors the Soap Box Derby,  including a single lay-back racer standing on its nose inside of a glass-enclosed display case.

rows.Name: Wheels Through Time Motorcycle Museum
rows.Notes: In 2025 two Derby cars were accepted to the museum, donated by their builder/owner George Freeman from Canton, North Carolina ,  who raced in 1952  and 1953.

rows.Name: Wisconsin Historical Museum
rows.Notes: Hosted an exhibit titled Zoom! Whiz! Wow! A High-Speed History of Madison's Soap Box Derby , which ran July 26 through September 11, 2010. Included were memorabilia, trophies, photos of boys that participated, and some cars, including one by 1957 Madison Champion Van Steiner.

rows.Name: Ypsilanti Automotive Heritage Museum
rows.Notes: Has a car (pictured) piloted by 1950 Ypsilanti, Michigan entry Bill Nickels.

List of films about the Titanic > Documentaries

rows.Title: Search for the Titanic
rows.Notes: Narrated by Orson Welles , documents Jack Grimm's July 1980 expedition .

rows.Title: Return to the Titanic
rows.Notes: Narrated by James Drury , documents Jack Grimm's June 1981 expedition .

rows.Title: In Search of Titanic
rows.Notes: A compilation film featuring footage from Search for the Titanic and Return to the Titanic .

rows.Title: Secrets of the Titanic
rows.Notes: Documents the finding of the wreck of the Titanic and the 1986 expedition led by Robert Ballard to find the Titanic

rows.Title: Titanic: The Nightmare and the Dream
rows.Notes: This film shows the Titanic and the work carried out by Bob Ballard and his team when they discovered the historic vessel at the bottom of the Atlantic ocean.

rows.Title: Titanic: The Complete Story
rows.Notes: Four hour documentary in two parts: Death of a Dream (origin of the Titanic, and its tragic sinking. Includes interviews with survivors), and The Legend Lives on (the legacy of the Titanic, and the 1985 discovery of the ship by Robert Ballard). Considered by many experts as the definitive documentary of the Titanic.

rows.Title: The Investigation Begins
rows.Notes: Documents the first, failed attempt to recover "the big piece" of the Titanic ' s hull

rows.Title: Anatomy of a Disaster
rows.Notes: Documents an expedition to the Titanic to determine the effects of microbes on the wreck, document the damage from the iceberg, and test the strength of Titanic ' s steel

rows.Title: Titanic: Untold Stories
rows.Notes: Historians retell the stories and experiences of the passengers from submersibles above the Titanic

rows.Title: Deep Inside Titanic
rows.Notes: Explores inside the Titanic with mini-subs

rows.Title: Titanic: Answers from the Abyss
rows.Notes: Efforts to document the entire wreck in a photomosaic, explores the breakup angle of the ship, the effect of watertight doors and the sinking of the bow section to the sea floor

rows.Title: Titanic: 90 Years Below
rows.Notes: Documents the efforts to find, explore and document the Titanic wreck, and the technology developed to find her... including a 2001 expedition to document the Titanic wreck with HD cameras

rows.Title: Modern Marvels: Titanic Tech
rows.Notes: Explores the technology used aboard the Titanic

rows.Title: Ghosts of the Abyss
rows.Notes: James Cameron returns to the Titanic with select cast members from the 1997 movie to explore more of the wreck

rows.Title: Last Mysteries of the Titanic with James Cameron
rows.Notes: Expedition with James Cameron to explore the interior of the wreck of the Titanic and document the condition of many unseen areas such as the Turkish baths and First Class Boarding Entrance

rows.Title: Titanic: Birth of a Legend
rows.Notes: Dramatization of the construction of the Titanic at Harland & Wolfe Shipyard, with many photographs of the ship and her sister Olympic under construction

rows.Title: Seconds From Disaster: Sinking of the Titanic
rows.Notes: Dramatization explaining how the "Unsinkable" ship sunk.

rows.Title: Titanic's Achilles Heel
rows.Notes: Documentary explores the theory that Titanic ' s expansion joints contributed to the breakup of the hull

rows.Title: Titanic: Ballard's Secret Mission
rows.Notes: Documentary reveals the true purpose of Robert Ballard's expedition to find the Titanic was a secret mission by the US Navy

rows.Title: What Sank Titanic
rows.Notes: Explains how the mechanical sophistication of the Titanic was beaten by an iceberg. Recreations and historical analysis explore the mysteries of the tragedy.

rows.Title: Titanic at 100: Mystery Solved
rows.Notes: Explores the possibility that Titanic had a fatal flaw that doomed the ship.

rows.Title: Titanic: Case Closed (British/international title) /Titanic's Final Mystery (American title)
rows.Notes: Presents a new theory why Titanic was unable to avoid the iceberg, and why nearby ships seemed to ignore the Titanic , and were even uncertain whether the lights they saw were the Titanic

rows.Title: Titanic: The Final Word with James Cameron
rows.Notes: James Cameron presents a new analysis and theory into the sequence of the sinking and breakup of the Titanic , informed by a paper by J.W. Stettler of the USCG

rows.Title: Save the Titanic with Bob Ballard
rows.Notes: Bob Ballard examines the damage to the wreck from repeated expeditions and implores that the wreck be protected by international agreements to prevent looting

rows.Title: Back to the Titanic
rows.Notes: First Expedition to return to the Titanic in nearly 15 years (claimed) examines the worsening state of decay of the wreck

rows.Title: Titanic's Lost Evidence
rows.Notes: Examines the notes of Lord Mersey from original 1912 British inquiry

rows.Title: Mysteries from the Grave: The Titanic
rows.Notes: Interviews with survivors' family also features Titanic honor and glory

rows.Title: How It Really Happened: Titanic
rows.Notes: Reviews latest findings and addresses the Titan Submersible tragedy

rows.Title: Titanic: The Digital Resurrection/Titanic: The Digital Resurrection: Beyond the Wreck (extended version)
rows.Notes: New examination of the tragedy through analysis of "Digital Twin"

rows.Title: Titanic Sinks Tonight
rows.Notes: Four-episode docudrama relating personal accounts of the survivors

table_name.header_chain: List of films about the Titanic > Television movies and notable episodes

rows.Title: "The Sinking of the Titanic: You Are There" You Are There
rows.Cast: Tod Hunter Klieth Roberts Harlow Wilkoff
rows.Notes: Episode of a CBS program called You Are There .

rows.Title: "The Titanic Incident" Screen Directors Playhouse
rows.Cast: Leo Genn , May Wynn , and Philip Reed
rows.Notes: Television episode of Screen Directors Playhouse set aboard the Titanic .

rows.Title: " A Night to Remembe r " Kraft Television Theatre
rows.Cast: Bradford Dillman Neil North
rows.Notes: Live TV adaptation of Walter Lord 's 1955 book of the same name ; narrated by Claude Rains .

rows.Title: "The Unsinkable Molly Brown" Telephone Time
rows.Cast: Cloris Leachman
rows.Notes: Short segment (using footage from the 1943 German film) from the TV version of John Nesbitt 's Passing Parade series. Leachman would again play the same role in S.O.S. Titanic (1979).

rows.Title: "Night of April 14th" Alcoa Presents: One Step Beyond
rows.Cast: Patrick Macnee Barbara Lord Isobel Elsom
rows.Notes: Purported docudrama relating stories of premonitions and nightmares preceding the disaster. The scene of the Titanic hitting the iceberg is from the 1937 drama film History Is Made at Night of the fictional ocean liner SS Princess Irene .

rows.Title: "I Heard You Calling Me" Way Out
rows.Cast: Constance Ford Neil Fitzgerald Anthony Dawson
rows.Notes: A woman planning to elope with a married man is invited on a free ocean cruise – by the ghost of the man's mother, who died on the Titanic .

rows.Title: "Rendezvous With Yesterday" The Time Tunnel
rows.Cast: James Darren Robert Colbert
rows.Notes: In the first episode of the series, the time travelers arrive on board the Titanic one day before the pending disaster. They try to warn the captain, but disbelieving them, he has them locked up and they narrowly avoid going down with the ship. Some footage and sets from the 1953 film are included in the episode.

rows.Title: "Lone Survivor" Night Gallery
rows.Cast: John Colicos Torin Thatcher Hedley Mattingly
rows.Notes: This story in the anthology series was written by Rod Serling .  A survivor in a Titanic lifeboat is discovered – three years after the event,  by the Lusitania .

rows.Title: "Miss Forrest",  "A House Divided"  Upstairs, Downstairs
rows.Cast: Rachel Gurney Patsy Smart Meg Wynn Owen David Langton Simon Williams Gordon Jackson Jean Marsh
rows.Notes: The series' 3rd season opens with "Miss Forrest" where it is learned that two main characters are aboard the Titanic . Mistress Lady Marjorie Bellamy (Gurney) and her maid, Miss Roberts (Smart) are both presumed dead. In the next episode, "A House Divided", it is learned that the maid survives, but is in emotional shock.  Eventually she relates how her mistress died on the Titanic .

rows.Title: S.O.S. Titanic
rows.Cast: David Janssen Cloris Leachman
rows.Notes: Depiction of the doomed 1912 voyage from the perspective of three distinct groups of passengers in First, Second, and Third Class.  Some characters are based on historical figures. Shorter version released theatrically in Europe.  The scenes of the ship sinking are colorized footage from A Night to Remember . Some scenes were filmed aboard the TSS Manxman and the RMS Queen Mary . This was the first Titanic film to be released in color .

rows.Title: "Voyagers of the Titanic" Voyagers!
rows.Cast: Jon-Erik Hexum Meeno Peluce
rows.Notes: Bogg and Jeff find themselves aboard the doomed Titanic .  Jeff wants to prevent the disaster, but Bogg warns him he can't: it is destined to happen.  Although failing to prevent the disaster, they save the Mona Lisa from being lost with the ship. Footage of the ship sinking was cut from the opening from Raise The Titanic . Also contains colorized footage of the iceberg and the Titanic from the 1953 film, stock footage of the RMS Queen Mary and some scenes filmed aboard the Queen Mary .

rows.Title: "Terror on the Titanic" Superfriends
rows.Notes: During a diving exploration on the Titanic wreck two divers were attacked by algae monsters caused by a mutation from the ship's wreckage when it sank. When Aquaman and Black Vulcan was sent over, the algae monsters turn the Titanic into a living monster that eats boats and went on a rampage on Newfondland. The Titanic-monster was defeated by Aquaman and Black Vulcan when they tricked it into crashing into a iceberg and made it sank again as a result.

rows.Title: Titanic - Nachspiel einer Katastrophe
rows.Cast: Hans Korte Volkert Kraeft Arthur Brauss
rows.Notes: ( Titanic – Aftermath of a disaster ), German TV courtroom drama centered on the United States Senate inquiry into the sinking of the Titanic .

rows.Title: Titanic
rows.Cast: Peter Gallagher George C. Scott Catherine Zeta-Jones Tim Curry
rows.Notes: This two-part television drama was the first depiction to show the Titanic splitting in two.

rows.Title: No Greater Love
rows.Cast: Kelly Rutherford
rows.Notes: Romance in which a young woman takes charge of her young siblings, upon losing her fiancé and parents in the disaster. Based on the Danielle Steel novel of the same name . The scenes of the ship sinking include footage from S.O.S. Titanic ; as in that film, some scenes were filmed aboard the Queen Mary .

rows.Title: " A Flight to Remember " Futurama
rows.Cast: Billy West Katey Sagal John DiMaggio
rows.Notes: The Planet Express team take a cruise on the largest starship ever built: the Titanic , which is torn in half and sucked into a black hole on its maiden voyage.

rows.Title: Britannic
rows.Cast: Edward Atterton Amanda Ryan Jacqueline Bisset John Rhys-Davies
rows.Notes: This television film is mostly about the sinking of the Titanic' s sister ship HMHS Britannic , but includes a Titanic survivor's flashback showing the Titanic sinking.

rows.Title: Thumbtanic
rows.Notes: Short film (26 min.) which parodies the 1997 film; part of the Thumbs! series

rows.Title: Titanic: Birth of a Legend
rows.Cast: Charles Dance Gordon Langford Rowe Charles Lawson Damian O'Hare Christopher Wright
rows.Notes: A 70-minute docudrama . The story focuses on the lives of the men who built Titanic and her sister ship RMS Olympic .

rows.Title: " Voyage of the Damned " Doctor Who
rows.Cast: David Tennant Kylie Minogue
rows.Notes: A luxury space cruiser called the Titanic , a pastiche of the ocean liner, crashes into the TARDIS . The Doctor works with a waitress to prevent a collision with Earth. In another episode entitled " Turn Left ", the Titanic crashes into London , killing millions.

rows.Title: "The Cursed Tuba Contingency" The Middleman
rows.Cast: Matt Keeslar Natalie Morales
rows.Notes: To avert dire consequences, the Middleman (Kesslar) and Wendy (Morales) must prevent a tuba from the Titanic from being played. In a flashback of the ship's sinking, footage from the 1943 film is used.

rows.Title: " The Mutants Are Revolting " Futurama
rows.Cast: Billy West Katey Sagal John DiMaggio
rows.Notes: In the sewers of New New York, the Planet Express crew discover the wreck of the Land Titanic , the largest articulated bus ever built, which sailed down Fifth Avenue in 2912 and struck a mail box and sank into the ground.

rows.Title: Titanic II
rows.Cast: Shane Van Dyke Brooke Burns
rows.Notes: A cruise liner sets sail on the 100th anniversary of the Titanic's doomed maiden voyage. When a tsunami hurls an iceberg into the ship's path, the crew and passengers struggle to avoid suffering the same fate as their predecessors.

rows.Title: " Episode One " Downton Abbey
rows.Notes: The first series opens with news of the Crawley family heir's death aboard the Titanic . Also referenced in Episode Six of Season 2 .

rows.Title: " My Heart Will Go On " Supernatural
rows.Cast: Jared Padalecki Jensen Ackles Misha Collins
rows.Notes: An angel changes history by averting the sinking of the Titanic , with unforeseen consequences.

rows.Title: Saving the Titanic
rows.Cast: David Wilmot Ciarán McMenamin Owen McDonnell
rows.Notes: 90-minute PBS docudrama . The story of the selfless engineers who kept the Titanic ' s essential electricity running during the tragedy.  Renamed as Heroes of the Titanic for UK broadcast on History .

rows.Title: Titanic
rows.Cast: Linus Roache Geraldine Somerville
rows.Notes: Four-part television drama based around characters present on the ship during its sinking. Shows the Titanic splitting in two at a much shallower angle, in accordance with a new breakup theory .

rows.Title: Titanic: Blood and Steel
rows.Cast: Neve Campbell Derek Jacobi
rows.Notes: 12-part television drama, telling the story of the construction of the ship. Contains numerous deviations from historical facts , mostly regarding the construction timeline.

rows.Title: Titanic: The Aftermath
rows.Cast: Jeremy Akerman John Dunsworth
rows.Notes: 90-minute docudrama on the lives of those who survived the sinking.

rows.Title: " Stewie, Chris, & Brian's Excellent Adventure " Family Guy
rows.Cast: Seth MacFarlane Alex Borstein Seth Green
rows.Notes: In the second half of the episode, Stewie , Brian , and Chris end up on the Titanic during their time travel adventure and manage to leave the ship during the sinking.

rows.Title: Titanic 666
rows.Cast: Joseph Gatt Jhey Castles Michael J. Chen
rows.Notes: Following the events of Titanic II , the Titanic III begins its maiden voyage to the original wreck site. However, the passengers start turning into ghosts after the ship's arrival, resulting in the sinking of the ship.

table_name.header_chain: Referendums in the United Kingdom > National referendums > 1975 European Communities membership referendum
table_name.caption: 1975 United Kingdom European Communities membership referendum
table_name.additional_text: The voters were asked to vote "Yes" or "No" on the question: "Do you think the United Kingdom should stay in the European Community (the Common Market)?"  In line with the outcome of the vote, the government took no further action and the United Kingdom remained a member of the European Communities which would later become the European Union .

table_name.header_chain: Referendums in the United Kingdom > National referendums > 2011 Alternative Vote referendum
table_name.caption: 2011 United Kingdom Alternative Vote referendum
table_name.additional_text: AV was rejected by 67% of voters with all but ten of the 440 voting areas voted "No" and the proposed legislation to introduce AV which was subject to the referendum was repealed.

table_name.header_chain: Referendums in the United Kingdom > National referendums > 2016 European Union membership referendum
table_name.caption: 2016 United Kingdom European Union membership referendum
table_name.additional_text: Of the 382 voting areas, 263 areas returned "majority" votes in favour of "Leave" whereas 119 areas returned "majority" votes in favour of "Remain" which included every Scottish council area and all but five of the London boroughs .
