rows.Name: Anadama bread
rows.Description: A traditional yeast bread of New England made with wheat flour, cornmeal , molasses and sometimes rye flour

rows.Name: Beaten biscuits
rows.Description: A dense biscuit, sometimes served with ham.  Before baking the dough is beaten extensively with a rolling pin or other blunt instrument.

rows.Name: Bulkie roll
rows.Description: A sandwich roll common in New England. Similar to a kaiser roll but sweeter

rows.Name: Cornbread
rows.Description: A quick bread made with cornmeal.

rows.Name: Frybread
rows.Description: Flat, fried bread with a fluffy interior and crunchy exterior, made with wheat flour, sugar, salt, and lard or vegetable oil.

rows.Name: Hot water corn bread
rows.Description: Cornbread made by mixing cornmeal and water and cooking the resulting batter in a skillet with cooking oil.

rows.Name: Johnnycakes
rows.Associated regions: East Coast , Southern United States , and Appalachia
rows.Description: Also known as hoecakes. Cornmeal flatbread , a dish of Native American origin.

rows.Name: New York–style bagel
rows.Description: Bagels which are larger and fatter than other styles of bagels

rows.Name: Pan de campo
rows.Description: A a flatbread made from wheat flour, baking powder, salt, a fat, and water. Traditionally cooked in a dutch oven .

rows.Name: Parker House roll
rows.Description: A bread roll that was invented at the Parker House Hotel in Boston during the 1870s.  It may be served as a side dish.

rows.Name: Pistolette
rows.Description: A pistolette is either of two bread-based dishes in Louisiana cuisine. One is a stuffed and fried bread roll (sometimes called stuffed pistolettes) in the Cajun areas around Lafayette . The other is a type of submarine shaped bread about half the size of a baguette that is popular in New Orleans for Vietnamese bánh mì and other sandwiches.

rows.Name: Texas toast
rows.Description: A type of thick-cut white bread, grilled with butter or margarine and often with garlic and other spices, and usually used as a side dish

table_name.header_chain: List of regional dishes of the United States > Regional dishes of the United States > Chicken dishes
table_name.additional_text: Main article: List of chicken dishes

rows.Name: Almond chicken
rows.Description: Chicken breaded in batter containing ground almonds, fried and served with almonds and onions.

rows.Name: Bourbon chicken
rows.Description: Chicken Marinated in soy sauce, brown sugar, ginger, bourbon whiskey, and sometimes honey.

rows.Name: Broasted chicken
rows.Description: Broasted chicken is pieces of chicken that have been battered and deep-fried in a pressure cooker .  The outside is very crispy and the inside is moist and juicy.  True broasted chicken is chicken that has been cooked using equipment and recipes supplied by the Broaster Company .

rows.Name: Buffalo wings
rows.Description: Chicken wing sections (wingettes and drumettes) that are deep-fried, unbreaded, and coated in a hot sauce made with cayenne pepper , vinegar, and butter. Usually served with celery or carrot sticks, and bleu cheese or ranch dressing for dipping.

rows.Name: Chicken and dumplings
rows.Description: Boiled chicken served with dumplings boiled in its broth

rows.Name: Chicken and waffles
rows.Description: The soul food version of chicken and waffles, popular in the South, pairs fried chicken with a breakfast waffle .  The Pennsylvania Dutch version, found in the Northeast, consists of a plain waffle with pulled, stewed chicken on top, covered in gravy.

rows.Name: Chicken Divan
rows.Description: A chicken casserole usually served with broccoli, almonds, and Mornay sauce . It was named after the place of its invention, the Divan Parisienne Restaurant in the New York City Chatham Hotel.

rows.Name: Chicken Francese
rows.Description: An Italian-American dish of flour-dredged, egg-dipped, sautéed chicken cutlets with a lemon-butter and sherry or white wine sauce.

rows.Name: Chicken Maryland
rows.Description: Fried chicken served with a cream gravy

rows.Name: Chicken mull
rows.Associated regions: North Carolina , South Carolina and Georgia
rows.Description: A traditional stew consisting of parboiled whole chicken in a cream or milk based broth, butter and seasoned with salt, pepper and other ingredients

rows.Name: Chicken parmesan
rows.Description: A breaded chicken breast covered in tomato sauce and mozzarella, parmesan and/or provolone.

rows.Name: Chicken riggies
rows.Description: An Italian-American pasta dish of chicken, rigatoni , and hot or sweet peppers, in a spicy cream and tomato sauce.

rows.Name: Chicken Vesuvio
rows.Description: Pieces of chicken on the bone, with potato wedges and peas, cooked with white wine, garlic, and olive oil.  An Italian American dish.

rows.Name: Country Captain
rows.Associated regions: Low Country of South Carolina and Georgia
rows.Description: Curried chicken over rice with onions, usually also with golden raisins and almonds.

rows.Name: Fried chicken
rows.Description: A dish consisting of chicken pieces that have been coated with seasoned flour or batter and pan-fried, deep-fried, pressure-fried, or air-fried. The breading adds a crisp coating or crust to the exterior of the chicken while retaining juices in the meat. Broiler chickens are most commonly used.

rows.Name: General Tso's chicken
rows.Description: A sweet and spicy Chinese-American deep-fried chicken dish in a sauce made of soy sauce, vinegar, and sugar, flavored with garlic and ginger.

rows.Name: Hawaiian haystack
rows.Description: A sauce with chunks of chicken, poured over steamed rice, and garnished with crispy chow mein noodles and pineapple.  Various optional condiments, such as coconut, diced bell peppers and tomatoes, and grated cheese are also often included.

rows.Name: Hot chicken
rows.Description: A portion of breast, thigh, or wing that has been marinated in buttermilk, floured, fried, and finally sauced using an oil-based paste that has been spiced with cayenne pepper.

rows.Name: King Ranch chicken
rows.Description: A Tex-Mex casserole made with shredded chicken, canned soup, canned tomatoes with chiles, cheese, and tortillas.

rows.Name: Lemon pepper wings
rows.Description: Fried chicken wings that have been heavily coated in lemon pepper seasoning. Lemon pepper wings can also be served "wet", i.e. with buffalo sauce .

rows.Name: Moravian chicken pie
rows.Description: A savory pie containing no vegetables and filled only with chicken meat and a small amount of thickened broth. Served with hot chicken gravy on top.

rows.Name: Springfield-style cashew chicken
rows.Description: Deep-fried pieces of chicken served over rice.  Topped with a sauce made of chicken broth, soy sauce, and oyster sauce, thickened with corn starch .  Garnished with unsalted cashews and sliced green onions.

table_name.header_chain: List of regional dishes of the United States > Regional dishes of the United States > Fish and seafood dishes
table_name.additional_text: Main articles: List of fish dishes and List of seafood dishes

rows.Name: California roll
rows.Description: A type of sushi that contains imitation crab (or rarely real crab), avocado, and cucumber.

rows.Name: Cioppino
rows.Description: Cioppino ( / tʃ oʊ ˈ p iː n oʊ / choh- PEE -noh ) is an Italian-American fish stew with tomatoes and a variety of fish and shellfish.

rows.Name: Clambake
rows.Description: Seafood and vegetables steamed between layers of seaweed over hot rocks on a beach.

rows.Name: Clam cakes
rows.Description: Fritter made from flour, water, baking powder, clam juice, and chopped or minced clams (usually quahogs) all mixed together, rolled into balls and deep fried.

rows.Name: Clam pie
rows.Description: A savory meat pie prepared using clams, especially quahogs , as a primary ingredient.

rows.Name: Clams casino
rows.Description: A clam served on a half clamshell, topped with breadcrumbs and crumbled bacon, and broiled.

rows.Name: Crab cakes
rows.Description: Crab meat and other ingredients (such as bread crumbs, milk, mayonnaise, eggs, and seasonings, particularly Old Bay Seasoning), traditionally deep-fried or sautéd , and increasingly often broiled.

rows.Name: Crab Rangoon
rows.Description: Filled crisp dumpling appetizers served primarily in American Chinese restaurants. The filling is made with a combination of cream cheese, crab meat or imitation crab meat, scallions or onion, garlic, and other flavorings.

rows.Name: Crawfish pie
rows.Description: A savory pie similar to a pot pie filled with crawfish .

rows.Name: Deviled crab
rows.Description: A crab meat croquette. Deviled crab croquettes originated in Tampa, Florida, where they were developed in the Spanish, Cuban and Italian immigrant community of Ybor City.

rows.Name: Étouffée
rows.Description: Étouffée ( / eɪ t uː ˈ f eɪ / ay-too- FAY ) is crawfish (or sometimes other shellfish such as shrimp or crabs) cooked using a technique called smothering , with roux , Cajun spices, and other ingredients, and served with rice.

rows.Name: Fish boil
rows.Description: Freshwater whitefish , potatoes , and onions are boiled in a large pot of salty water, with the fish and potatoes in wire baskets.  When the fish is ready, the fish oil, which has floated to the top, is removed, traditionally with burning kerosene.

rows.Name: Fried clams
rows.Description: Clams that have been dipped in milk, floured, and deep-fried. They are "to New England , what barbecue is to the South".  They tend to be served at seaside clam shacks (roadside restaurants).

rows.Name: Frogmore stew
rows.Associated regions: Low Country of South Carolina and Georgia
rows.Description: Frogmore stew, also known as low country boil, is a dish consisting of shell-on shrimp, smoked sausage, corn, and red potatoes all cooked together in a spice laden broth. It's typically served family style, on newspaper with lemon, cocktail sauce, and drawn butter.

rows.Name: Hangtown fry
rows.Description: Hangtown fry is a type of omelette made famous during the California Gold Rush in the 1850s. The most common version includes bacon and oysters combined with eggs, and fried together.

rows.Name: Lobster Newberg
rows.Description: An American seafood dish made from lobster, butter, cream, cognac , sherry , eggs, and cayenne pepper.

rows.Name: Lobster roll
rows.Description: A sandwich of lobster meat served in a top-loading hot dog bun.

rows.Name: Lox and schmear bagel
rows.Description: Lox and cream cheese (schmear) on a New York-style bagel. Often garnished with tomato, onion, cucumber, and/or capers.

rows.Name: Oysters Bienville
rows.Description: A traditional dish in New Orleans cuisine ,  it consists of filled, baked oysters . Ingredients include shrimp, mushrooms, bell peppers, sherry, a roux with butter, Parmesan cheese and other lighter cheese, as well as bread crumbs .

rows.Name: Oysters en brochette
rows.Description: A classic dish in New Orleans Creole cuisine,  raw oysters are skewered , alternating with pieces of partially cooked bacon . The entire dish is then broiled or breaded (usually with corn flour ) then either deep fried or sautéed

rows.Name: Oysters Rockefeller
rows.Description: Oysters on the half-shell that have been topped with various other ingredients (often parsley and other green herbs, a rich butter sauce and bread crumbs) and are then baked or broiled

rows.Name: Popcorn shrimp
rows.Description: Deep fried shrimp, eaten as a finger food like popcorn.

rows.Name: Rolled oyster
rows.Description: A baseball-sized seafood dish that is found only in and around Louisville, Kentucky. It consists of three raw oysters dipped in an egg-milk cornmeal batter called pastinga, rolled in cracker crumbs (hence the name), and deep fried.

rows.Name: Seattle roll
rows.Description: A sushi roll with salmon and cream cheese.

rows.Name: Shrimp and grits
rows.Associated regions: The South Carolina Lowcountry and other coastal areas of the Southeast
rows.Description: Grits with cooked shrimp added, usually served for breakfast.

rows.Name: Shrimp Creole
rows.Description: Cooked shrimp in a mixture of tomatoes, onions, celery, and bell peppers, spiced with hot pepper sauce or cayenne -based seasoning, and served over steamed or boiled white rice.

rows.Name: Shrimp DeJonghe
rows.Description: A casserole of large, peeled shrimp, soft breadcrumbs, and a rich sauce made with butter, garlic, and white wine or sherry.

rows.Name: Squid lū'au
rows.Description: Made with squid (or octopus), taro (lu'au) leaves, coconut milk, garlic, water, and Hawaiian salt .  (Squid lū'au is pictured at the very bottom of the image.)

rows.Name: Steamed clams
rows.Description: A seafood dish consisting of clams cooked by steaming. Usually made with small soft-shell clams (Mya arenaria) called 'steamers'.

rows.Name: Stuffies
rows.Associated regions: Rhode Island and elsewhere in New England
rows.Description: Also known as stuffed clams or stuffed quahogs. Quahog clams, minced and mixed with breadcrumbs and sometimes other ingredients, baked on the half-shell.

table_name.header_chain: List of regional dishes of the United States > Regional dishes of the United States > Potato dishes
table_name.additional_text: Main article: List of potato dishes

rows.Name: Disco fries
rows.Description: A dish of french fries topped with brown gravy and melted shredded cheese (typically mozzarella).

rows.Name: Funeral potatoes
rows.Description: A casserole of hash browns or grated/cubed potatoes, Cheddar or Parmesan cheese, cream soup or a cream sauce, and other ingredients, topped with corn flakes or crushed potato chips.

rows.Name: Jo Jo potatoes
rows.Description: Potato wedges that are fried in the same vat as chicken,  or that are coated in a seasoned flour and fried.

rows.Name: Potatoes O'Brien
rows.Associated regions: Boston, Massachusetts and Manhattan , New York
rows.Description: Pan-fried potatoes along with green and red bell peppers . Its origin is disputed;  it has been claimed that it originated in the early 20th century  from a Boston restaurant named Jerome's  and, during the same time period, from a Manhattan restaurant named Jack's.

rows.Name: Salt potatoes
rows.Description: As the potatoes cook, the salty water forms a crust on the skin and seals the potatoes so they never taste waterlogged

table_name.header_chain: List of regional dishes of the United States > Regional dishes of the United States > Rice dishes
table_name.additional_text: Main article: List of rice dishes

rows.Name: Charleston red rice
rows.Associated regions: The lowcountry of South Carolina and Georgia
rows.Description: Long grain rice cooked with crushed tomatoes, small bits of bacon or smoked pork sausage , celery, bell peppers, and onions.

rows.Name: Dirty rice
rows.Description: Rice cooked with small amounts of meat (traditionally chicken giblets ) which give it a dark color, along with onions, bell peppers, celery, and spices.

rows.Name: Halal over rice
rows.Description: Halal-slaughtered lamb or chicken over yellow rice , typically with white sauce and vegetables.

rows.Name: Hoppin' John
rows.Description: Rice cooked with black-eyed peas or field peas , chopped onion, and sliced bacon.  Sometimes country sausage , ham hock , fatback , or another type of meat is used instead of bacon.

rows.Name: Jambalaya
rows.Description: A dish of rice and meat in Louisiana Creole cuisine (often a combination of andouille sausage , chicken, and shrimp) cooked with vegetables and Louisiana Creole spices.

rows.Name: Red beans and rice
rows.Description: A dish in Louisiana Creole cuisine, it is prepared with kidney beans cooked with Louisiana Cajun spices, and often also cooked with ham and vegetables such as bell peppers, onions, and celery, served together with white rice.

rows.Name: Rice and gravy
rows.Description: Traditionally a brown gravy based on pan drippings, cooked with onions, bell peppers, celery, and seasonings, and served over steamed or boiled rice.  Now often made with various types of meats.

rows.Name: Seattle-style teriyaki
rows.Description: A comfort food originating in Seattle, it is characterized by fresh meat marinated in a sweet soy-ginger blend, grilled over an open flame, and finished with a drizzle of teriyaki sauce. Served with coleslaw-like salad and rice.

rows.Name: Spam musubi
rows.Description: A piece of grilled Spam on top of a rice ball , held together with a strip of nori .  This is similar to nigiri sushi , but with Spam instead of raw fish.

table_name.header_chain: List of regional dishes of the United States > Regional dishes of the United States > Salads
table_name.additional_text: Main article: List of salads

rows.Name: Celery Victor
rows.Description: Celery hearts simmered in a veal, chicken, or beef stock, chilled (often in a citrus or vinegar marinade), tossed with mild peppers, and sometimes served over lettuce.

rows.Name: Chinese chicken salad
rows.Description: A salad with chicken, Chinese noodles, lettuce, ginger, and sesame oil.

rows.Name: Cobb salad
rows.Description: A garden salad made from chopped salad greens ( iceberg lettuce , watercress , endives and Romaine lettuce ), tomato, crisp bacon, boiled, grilled or roasted (but not fried) chicken breast, hard-boiled egg, avocado, chives, Roquefort cheese, and red-wine vinaigrette .  Various stories exist recounting how the salad was invented.

rows.Name: Crab Louie
rows.Description: Iceberg lettuce with Dungeness crab or other crab meat, hard boiled eggs, tomatoes, and Louis dressing .

rows.Name: Frogeye salad
rows.Description: A pasta salad that is made with acini di pepe pasta, whipped topping and egg yolks. Fruit, such as mandarin oranges and pineapples , are often mixed in, and it is sometimes topped with marshmallows .

rows.Name: Lomi-lomi salmon
rows.Description: A fresh, cold Hawaiian side dish (or salad) served at luau celebrations, typically made by massaging salted, diced salmon with raw tomatoes, sweet onions, and sometimes green onions.

rows.Name: Michigan salad
rows.Description: A green salad topped with dried cherries or cranberries, blue cheese , vinaigrette , and sometimes apple slices.

rows.Name: Pittsburgh salad
rows.Description: A layered salad, often composed of lettuce, vegetables, grilled meat, shredded cheese, ranch dressing, and most notably, french fries.

rows.Name: Poke
rows.Description: Poke ( / ˈ p oʊ k eɪ / POH -kay ) is a raw seafood salad served as an appetizer in Hawaiian cuisine.  It is most commonly made with yellowfin tuna , salty seaweed, and sweet onions.

rows.Name: Seven-layer salad
rows.Description: A salad with seven layers, usually composed of iceberg lettuce, peas, tomatoes, onions, Cheddar cheese, bacon, and mayonnaise.  Served in a glass bowl with high sides.

rows.Name: Shrimp Louie
rows.Description: Iceberg lettuce with Pacific pink shrimp or other small boiled and shelled shrimp, hard boiled eggs, tomatoes, and Louis dressing ; basically the same ingredients as a Crab Louie salad, but with shrimp instead of Dungeness crab

rows.Name: Taco salad
rows.Description: A fried flour tortilla shell stuffed with shredded iceberg lettuce and topped with diced tomatoes, shredded Cheddar cheese, sour cream, guacamole, and salsa. Topped with ground beef, shredded chicken, beans, and/or Spanish rice .

rows.Name: Texas caviar
rows.Description: A bean salad consisting of black-eyed peas lightly pickled in a vinaigrette-style dressing, often eaten as a dip accompaniment to tortilla chips.

rows.Name: Waldorf salad
rows.Description: First created between 1893 and 1896 at the Waldorf Hotel in New York City, it is generally made of fresh apples, celery and walnuts, dressed in mayonnaise.

rows.Name: Whitefish salad
rows.Description: A salad of smoked freshwater whitefish and mayonnaise. An Ashkenazi Jewish staple.

table_name.header_chain: List of regional dishes of the United States > Regional dishes of the United States > Sandwiches
table_name.additional_text: See also: List of sandwiches

rows.Name: Bacon egg and cheese
rows.Description: A sandwich made with bacon, eggs (usually fried or scrambled), and cheese on a kaiser roll . Typically with salt, pepper, and ketchup.

rows.Name: Beef Manhattan
rows.Description: An open-faced sandwich of roast beef and gravy , served with mashed potatoes .

rows.Name: Beef on weck
rows.Description: Thin-sliced roast beef on a Kümmelweck roll (a Kaiser roll topped with caraway seeds and salt).  The cut face of the top half of the roll may be dipped in the jus from the roast. Horseradish is usually provided for the diner to spread to taste on the top half of the roll.

rows.Name: Chopped Cheese
rows.Description: Ground beef with onions, topped by melted cheese, and served with lettuce, tomatoes and condiments on a hero roll.

rows.Name: Chow mein sandwich
rows.Description: A brown gravy-based chow mein mixture placed between halves of a hamburger-style bun.

rows.Name: Club sandwich
rows.Description: A three-layer sandwich consisting of three slices of bread (traditionally toasted), sliced poultry, fried bacon, lettuce, tomato, and mayonnaise.

rows.Name: Cuban sandwich
rows.Description: A pressed sandwich made with sliced ham and roasted pork, Swiss cheese, pickles, mustard, and sometimes Genoa salami, on Cuban bread .   Medianoche sandwiches are very closely related.

rows.Name: Denver sandwich
rows.Description: Also known as a Western sandwich.  A Denver omelette (scrambled eggs with diced ham, onions, and green bell peppers) on two pieces of bread.

rows.Name: Eggs Benedict
rows.Description: The two halves of a toasted English muffin topped with Canadian bacon , poached eggs , and hollandaise sauce .  Claims exist that it was invented at the Waldorf Hotel in New York City in 1894, and another claim is that it was first made by Edward P. Montgomery on behalf of commodore E. C. Benedict.

rows.Name: Fluffernutter
rows.Description: Made with peanut butter and marshmallow fluff , usually served on white bread

rows.Name: Fool's Gold Loaf
rows.Description: A French bread, baked and hollowed out, and filled with a jar of peanut butter, a jar of grape jelly, and a pound of bacon.

rows.Name: French dip
rows.Description: Thin-sliced beef served on a French roll, often topped with Swiss cheese and onions. Traditionally, the bread is dipped in the beef juice that results from cooking, though it's not unusual for the jus to be served on the side.

rows.Name: Fried-brain sandwich
rows.Description: A sandwich made with heavily battered sliced calves' brains , deep fried and served on sliced bread.

rows.Name: Gerber sandwich
rows.Description: An open-faced sandwich of a half section of Italian or French bread, spread with garlic butter and topped with ham and either Provel or Provolone cheese, seasoned with a sprinkling of paprika, and then toasted.

rows.Name: Heel sandwich
rows.Description: A thick, crusty "heel" of a loaf of Italian bread hollowed out and stuffed with meatballs, marinara sauce, and melted provolone or mozzarella cheese that is then broiled.

rows.Name: Horseshoe sandwich
rows.Description: An open-faced sandwich of thick-sliced toasted bread, a hamburger patty or other meat, French fries, and a cheese sauce that is somewhat similar to Welsh rarebit .

rows.Name: Hot brown
rows.Description: An open-faced sandwich of turkey with sliced tomatoes on thick-cut toast, covered with Mornay sauce and topped with bacon, and baked or broiled until the bread is crisp and the sauce begins to brown.

rows.Name: Italian beef
rows.Description: A sandwich of thin slices of seasoned roast beef, dripping with meat juices, on a dense, long Italian-style roll.

rows.Name: Jibarito
rows.Description: A jibarito ( / ˌ h iː b ə ˈ r iː t oʊ / HEE -bə- REE -toh ) is a sandwich, inspired by the cuisine of Puerto Rico , made with flattened, fried green plantains instead of bread.  Generally with a thin steak filling, or sometimes chicken or pork.  Usually topped with garlic-flavored mayonnaise, lettuce, and tomato.

rows.Name: Limburger sandwich
rows.Description: Limburger cheese on bread

rows.Name: Mother-in-law
rows.Description: A tamale in a hot dog bun, covered with chili .

rows.Name: Muffuletta
rows.Description: A sandwich on a muffuletta bread, a large, round, and light Italian bread with sesame seeds.  It's filled with various meats and cheeses, usually including ham , salami , mortadella , Swiss cheese , and provolone , with olive salad spread on the bread.

rows.Name: Pastrami on rye
rows.Description: Pastrami on rye bread, typically with spicy brown mustard.

rows.Name: Pepper and egg sandwich
rows.Description: Scrambled eggs and grilled bell peppers on French bread.

rows.Name: Pilgrim sandwich
rows.Description: Also known as a Thanksgiving sandwich.  Made with sliced turkey, stuffing, cranberry sauce, and sometimes cheese and other ingredients.

rows.Name: Pit beef sandwich
rows.Description: A sandwich of charcoal-roasted beef, sliced and served rare on a Kaiser roll .

rows.Name: Po' boy
rows.Description: A submarine sandwich on a wide piece of French bread that is crunchy on the outside and light on the inside.  Popular fillings include fried seafood such as shrimp, oysters, or catfish, and the more traditional roast beef with brown gravy.  Usually topped ("dressed") with shredded lettuce, tomatoes, pickles, and mayonnaise.

rows.Name: Pork tenderloin sandwich
rows.Description: A large, thin pork cutlet , breaded and deep-fried, served on a bun.

rows.Name: Primanti Sandwich
rows.Description: Grilled meat, melted cheese, an oil & vinegar-based coleslaw, tomato slices, and French fries between two thick slices of Italian bread.

rows.Name: Reuben sandwich
rows.Associated regions: New York City and Omaha, Nebraska
rows.Description: A hot sandwich composed of corned beef , Swiss cheese , sauerkraut , and Russian or Thousand Island dressing, grilled between slices of rye bread .  One account holds that Reuben Kulakofsky of Omaha, Nebraska invented the sandwich, and another holds that it was invented by Arnold Reuben at Reuben's Restaurant in New York City.

rows.Name: Runza
rows.Description: A hand-held meat pie similar to a bierock , with a yeast dough bread pocket and a filling of ground beef, shredded cabbage, and seasonings.

rows.Name: Sailor sandwich
rows.Description: A sandwich of grilled knackwurst, hot pastrami, melted Swiss cheese, and spicy mustard on rye bread.

rows.Name: Sloppy joe
rows.Description: In most of the U.S., a sloppy joe is a sandwich of ground beef and tomato sauce, with onion and spices, served on a hamburger bun.  But in North Jersey, a sloppy joe is a double decker thin sliced rye bread sandwich made with one or more types of sliced deli meat, such as turkey, ham, pastrami , corned beef , roast beef , or sliced beef tongue , along with Swiss cheese , coleslaw , and Russian dressing .

rows.Name: Spaghetti sandwich
rows.Description: A sandwich prepared with cooked spaghetti, sauce and bread.

rows.Name: Spiedie
rows.Description: A spiedie ( / ˈ s p iː d i / SPEE -dee ) is a sandwich of marinated cubes of lamb, chicken, pork, or beef served on Italian bread or white bread.

rows.Name: St. Paul sandwich
rows.Description: An egg foo young patty on white bread, with dill pickle slices, lettuce, tomatoes, and mayonnaise.

rows.Name: Submarine sandwich
rows.Description: Also known as a sub, wedge, hoagie, hero, grinder, baguette and other names, it originated in several different Italian American communities in the Northeastern United States from the late 19th to mid-20th centuries.  A long roll of bread split widthwise into two pieces, and filled with a variety of meats, cheeses, vegetables, seasonings, and sauces.

rows.Name: Tavern sandwich
rows.Description: Also known as a loosemeat sandwich,  it contains crumbled, unseasoned ground beef on a bun, mixed with sauteed onions, and sometimes topped with pickles, ketchup and mustard.

rows.Name: Tomato sandwich
rows.Description: Ripe-to-overripe non-commercially grown tomatoes, mayonnaise, salt, and pepper on soft commercial white bread.

rows.Name: Turkey Devonshire
rows.Description: A hot open-faced sandwich on toasted bread with hot turkey, bacon, tomatoes, and a cheese sauce, similar to a Hot brown .

table_name.header_chain: List of regional dishes of the United States > Regional dishes of the United States > Soups and stews
table_name.additional_text: Main articles: List of soups and List of stews

rows.Name: Bookbinder soup
rows.Description: Seafood soup made with common snapping turtle meat.

rows.Name: Booyah
rows.Description: A thick soup that often requires up to two days and multiple cooks to prepare; it is cooked in specially designed "booyah kettles" and usually meant to serve hundreds or even thousands of people.

rows.Name: Brunswick stew
rows.Description: A stew based on tomatoes, local beans and vegetables, and chicken in recent times; originally, small game meat such as squirrel, rabbit or opossum was used instead.

rows.Name: Burgoo
rows.Description: A spicy stew ,  typically using game or game birds, similar to Irish or Mulligan stew , often served with cornbread or corn muffins .

rows.Name: Catfish stew
rows.Description: A dish that consists of catfish fillets. which are heavily boiled so that they fall apart, and is then combined with crushed tomatoes, potatoes, and onions.

rows.Name: Chili con carne
rows.Description: Originated in Texas and is the official dish of the U.S. state of Texas, as designated by the House Concurrent Resolution Number 18 of the 65th Texas Legislature during its regular session in 1977.

rows.Name: Conch soup
rows.Description: A soup made from conch, a type of sea snail.

rows.Name: Corn chowder
rows.Description: A corn-based chowder with cream.

rows.Name: Cream of crab soup
rows.Description: A dish from the Eastern Shore of Maryland . It is made with lump Maryland blue crab meat, onion, whole milk and/or half and half (milk and cream blend), butter, either flour or corn starch as a thickener, and Old Bay as the main seasoning.

rows.Name: Gumbo
rows.Description: A meat or seafood soup or stew thickened with okra or filé .

rows.Name: Manhattan-style clam chowder
rows.Description: Clams cooked in a red broth with tomatoes for flavor and color.

rows.Name: Maryland crab soup
rows.Description: A soup made with lump Maryland crab meat, tomatoes, corn, potato, cellery or celery leaves, peas, onion, and Old Bay . The main liquid of the soup can be water, shellfish stock , or fish stock. Other seasoning options used include red pepper, bay leaf , thyme , garlic, dry mustard,  and/or salt.

rows.Name: Matzah ball soup
rows.Description: Staple food on Passover . The Matzah ball dumplings are traditionally served in chicken broth with sliced carrots, garnished with chopped parsley. Matzo balls are also referred to as knaidel or knaedle .

rows.Name: New England-style clam chowder
rows.Description: A milk- or cream-based chowder of potatoes, onion, and clams.

rows.Name: Oyster stew
rows.Description: A stew made with oysters.

rows.Name: Peanut soup
rows.Description: A soup made from peanuts, often with various other ingredients.

rows.Name: Philadelphia Pepper Pot
rows.Description: A thick stew of beef tripe , vegetables, pepper and other seasonings.

rows.Name: Saimin
rows.Description: Traditionally consisting of soft wheat egg noodles served in a hot dashi garnished with diced green onions and a thin slice of kamaboko , modern versions of saimin include additional toppings such as char siu , sliced Spam , sliced egg , bok choy , mushrooms , or shredded nori .

rows.Name: She-crab soup
rows.Description: A seafood soup made with blue crab meat, crab roe , and crab stock mixed with heavy cream and dry sherry.

rows.Name: Sonofabitch stew
rows.Description: A cowboy dish of the Old West.  A beef stew, the ingredients of which depended on availability.  Sometimes made with offal from a calf .

rows.Name: Vichyssoise
rows.Description: Vichyssoise ( / v iː ʃ iː ˈ s w ɑː z / vee-shee- SWAHZ ) is a thick soup made of puréed leeks , onions, potatoes, cream, and chicken stock .  Its origins is a subject of debate among culinary historians; Julia Child calls it "an American invention",  whereas others observe that "the origin of the soup is questionable in whether it's genuinely French or an American creation".

rows.Name: Yaka mein
rows.Description: A soup that combines influences of Chinese and Creole cuisine.  Stewed beef in beef-based broth with noodles, garnished with half a hard-boiled egg and chopped green onions, with Creole or Cajun seasoning.

table_name.header_chain: List of regional dishes of the United States > Regional dishes of the United States > Steak dishes
table_name.additional_text: Main article: List of steak dishes

rows.Name: Beef and broccoli
rows.Description: Stir-fried sliced steak an broccoli florets with oyster or soy sauce and aromatics such as garlic and ginger.

rows.Name: Cheesesteak
rows.Description: Also known as a Philly cheesesteak.  Thinly sliced beef and melted cheese (generally Cheez Whiz , American cheese , or Provolone ) on a hoagie roll , typically with sauteed onions and other seasonings.

rows.Name: Chicken fried steak
rows.Description: A breaded cutlet dish consisting of a piece of tenderized cube steak coated with seasoned flour and pan fried .

rows.Name: Delmonico steak
rows.Description: A method of preparation from one of several cuts of beef (typically the Rib Cut) prepared Delmonico style, made by Delmonico's Restaurant in New York City during the mid-19th century.

rows.Name: Finger steaks
rows.Description: Small strips of steak (usually sirloin), battered with a tempura-like batter and deep-fried in oil. Typically served with French fries and fry sauce , and a thick piece of buttered toast.

rows.Name: Pork steak
rows.Description: A steak made from a slice of pork shoulder ; often smoked or slow-cooked with barbecue sauce.

rows.Name: Steak de Burgo
rows.Description: Usually consists of a beef tenderloin either topped with butter, garlic, and Italian herbs , or served in a sauce consisting of those same ingredients.

rows.Name: Steak Diane
rows.Description: A pan-fried beefsteak with a sauce made from the seasoned pan juices, generally prepared in restaurants tableside, and flambéed . It does not appear in the classics of French cuisine, and was probably invented in mid-20th century New York City as part of the fad for tableside-flambéed dishes.

rows.Name: Steamed cheeseburger
rows.Description: Ground beef is steamed on a tray to create a juicy patty without any grease. Steamed cheese, raw onion and mustard toppings are added afterwards.

table_name.caption: Examples of coinage legends
table_name.additional_text: As the legends became longer, words in the inscriptions were often abbreviated so that they could fit on the coin; identical legends have often been abbreviated in different ways depending upon the size and decoration of the coin.

rows.Latin text: EDWARD DEI GRA REX ANGL Z FRANC D HYB(E)
rows.English text: Edward III , by the grace of God King of England and France, Lord of Ireland

rows.Latin text: EDWARD DEI GRA REX ANGL DNS HYB Z ACQ
rows.English text: Edward , by the grace of God King of England, Lord of Ireland and Aquitaine
rows.Notes: Used after the Treaty of Brétigny (1360) when Edward III temporarily gave up his claim to the French throne .

rows.Latin text: EDWARD DEI G REX ANG Z FRA DNS HYB Z ACT
rows.English text: Edward , by the grace of God King of England and France, Lord of Ireland and Aquitaine
rows.Notes: Used after Anglo-French relations broke down and Edward III resumed his claim.

rows.Latin text: HENRICUS VII DEI GRATIA REX ANGLIÆ & FRANCIÆ
rows.English text: Henry VII by the Grace of God, King of England and France
rows.Notes: France had been claimed by the English continuously since 1369.

rows.Latin text: HENRICUS VIII DEI GRATIA REX ANGLIÆ & FRANCIÆ
rows.English text: Henry VIII by the Grace of God, King of England and France
rows.Notes: The Arabic numeral 8 was also used instead of the Roman VIII.

rows.Latin text: HENRICUS VIII DEI GRATIA ANGLIÆ FRANCIÆ & HIBERNIÆ REX
rows.English text: Henry VIII by the Grace of God, Of England, France and Ireland, King
rows.Notes: Used after Henry VIII made Ireland a kingdom in 1541. The Arabic numeral 8 was also used instead of the Roman VIII.

rows.Latin text: PHILIPPUS ET MARIA DEI GRATIA REX & REGINA
rows.English text: Philip and Mary by the Grace of God, King and Queen
rows.Notes: The names of the realms were omitted from the coin for reasons of space.

rows.Latin text: ELIZABETH DEI GRATIA ANGLIÆ FRANCIÆ ET HIBERNIÆ REGINA
rows.English text: Elizabeth , by the Grace of God, of England, France, and Ireland, Queen

rows.Latin text: IACOBUS DEI GRATIA MAGNÆ BRITANNIÆ FRANCIÆ ET HIBERNIÆ REX
rows.English text: James , by the Grace of God, of Great Britain, France, and Ireland, King
rows.Notes: James, King of Scotland, by succeeding to the English throne united the two kingdoms in his person; he dubbed the combination of the two kingdoms "Great Britain" (the name of the whole island) though they remained legislatively distinct for more than a century afterwards.

rows.Latin text: CAROLUS DEI GRATIA MAGNÆ BRITANNIÆ FRANCIÆ ET HIBERNIÆ REX
rows.English text: Charles , by the Grace of God, of Great Britain, France, and Ireland, King

rows.Latin text: OLIVARIUS DEI GRATIA REIPUBLICÆ ANGLIÆ SCOTIÆ HIBERNIÆ & CETERORUM PROTECTOR
rows.English text: Oliver , by the Grace of God, of the Commonwealth of England, Scotland, Ireland etc., Protector
rows.Notes: Cromwell ruled as a monarch but did not claim the title of king.

rows.Latin text: CAROLUS II DEI GRATIA MAGNÆ BRITANNIÆ FRANCIÆ ET HIBERNIÆ REX
rows.English text: Charles II , by the Grace of God, of Great Britain, France, and Ireland, King

rows.Latin text: IACOBUS II DEI GRATIA MAGNÆ BRITANNIÆ FRANCIÆ ET HIBERNIÆ REX
rows.English text: James II , by the Grace of God, of Great Britain, France, and Ireland, King

rows.Latin text: GULIELMUS ET MARIA DEI GRATIA MAGNÆ BRITANNIÆ FRANCIÆ ET HIBERNIÆ REX ET REGINA
rows.English text: William and Mary by the Grace of God, of Great Britain, France, and Ireland, King and Queen
rows.Notes: The spouses William and Mary ruled jointly.

rows.Latin text: GULIELMUS III DEI GRATIA MAGNÆ BRITANNIÆ FRANCIÆ ET HIBERNIÆ REX
rows.English text: William III by the Grace of God, of Great Britain, France, and Ireland, King
rows.Notes: William continued to rule alone after his wife's death.

rows.Latin text: ANNA DEI GRATIA MAGNÆ BRITANNIÆ FRANCIÆ ET HIBERNIÆ REGINA
rows.English text: Anne by the Grace of God, of Great Britain, France, and Ireland, Queen

rows.Latin text: GEORGIUS DEI GRATIA MAGNÆ BRITANNIÆ FRANCIÆ ET HIBERNIÆ REX FIDEI DEFENSOR BRUNSVICENSIS ET LUNEBURGENSIS DUX SACRI ROMANI IMPERII ARCHITHESAURARIUS ET ELECTOR
rows.English text: George by the Grace of God, of Great Britain, France, and Ireland King, Defender of the Faith, of Brunswick and Lüneburg Duke, of the Holy Roman Empire Archtreasurer and Elector
rows.Notes: George I added the titles he already possessed as Elector of Hanover . He also added the title " Defender of the Faith ", which had been borne by the English kings since Henry VIII , but which had previously only rarely appeared on coins.

rows.Latin text: GEORGIUS II DEI GRATIA MAGNÆ BRITANNIÆ FRANCIÆ ET HIBERNIÆ REX FIDEI DEFENSOR BRUNSVICENSIS ET LUNEBURGENSIS DUX SACRI ROMANI IMPERII ARCHITHESAURARIUS ET ELECTOR
rows.English text: George II by the Grace of God, of Great Britain, France, and Ireland King, Defender of the Faith, of Brunswick and Lüneburg Duke, of the Holy Roman Empire Archtreasurer and Elector

rows.Latin text: GEORGIUS III DEI GRATIA MAGNÆ BRITANNIÆ FRANCIÆ ET HIBERNIÆ REX FIDEI DEFENSOR BRUNSVICENSIS ET LUNEBURGENSIS DUX SACRI ROMANI IMPERII ARCHITHESAURARIUS ET ELECTOR
rows.English text: George III by the Grace of God, of Great Britain, France, and Ireland King, Defender of the Faith, of Brunswick and Lüneburg Duke, of the Holy Roman Empire Archtreasurer and Elector

rows.Latin text: GEORGIUS III DEI GRATIA BRITANNIARUM REX FIDEI DEFENSOR
rows.English text: George III, by the Grace of God, of the Britains King, Defender of the Faith
rows.Notes: The Acts of Union united Great Britain and Ireland into a single kingdom, represented on the coinage by the Latin genitive plural Britanniarum ("of the Britains", often abbreviated BRITT ). At the same time, the claim to the throne of France was dropped and other titles were omitted from the coinage.

rows.Latin text: GEORGIUS IIII DEI GRATIA BRITANNIARUM REX FIDEI DEFENSOR
rows.English text: George IV , by the Grace of God, of the Britains King, Defender of the Faith

rows.Latin text: GEORGIUS IV DEI GRATIA BRITANNIARUM REX FIDEI DEFENSOR
rows.English text: George IV , by the Grace of God, of the Britains King, Defender of the Faith

rows.Latin text: GULIELMUS IIII DEI GRATIA BRITANNIARUM REX FIDEI DEFENSOR
rows.English text: William IV , by the Grace of God, of the Britains King, Defender of the Faith

rows.Latin text: VICTORIA DEI GRATIA BRITANNIARUM REGINA FIDEI DEFENSOR
rows.English text: Victoria , by the Grace of God, of the Britains Queen, Defender of the Faith

rows.Latin text: VICTORIA DEI GRATIA BRITANNIARUM REGINA FIDEI DEFENSOR INDIÆ IMPERATRIX
rows.English text: Victoria , by the Grace of God, of the Britains Queen, Defender of the Faith, Empress of India
rows.Notes: Queen Victoria was granted the title "Empress of India" in 1876.

rows.Latin text: EDWARDUS VII DEI GRATIA BRITANNIARUM OMNIUM REX FIDEI DEFENSOR INDIÆ IMPERATOR
rows.English text: Edward VII , by the Grace of God, of all the Britains King, Defender of the Faith, Emperor of India
rows.Notes: Edward VII's coins added OMNIUM ("all") after "Britains" to imply a rule over the British overseas colonies as well as the United Kingdoms of England, Scotland, and Ireland.

rows.Latin text: GEORGIUS V DEI GRATIA BRITANNIARUM OMNIUM REX FIDEI DEFENSOR INDIÆ IMPERATOR
rows.English text: George V , by the Grace of God, of all the Britains King, Defender of the Faith, Emperor of India

rows.Latin text: EDWARDUS VIII DEI GRATIA BRITANNIARUM OMNIUM REX FIDEI DEFENSOR INDIÆ IMPERATOR
rows.English text: Edward VIII , by the Grace of God, of all the Britains King, Defender of the Faith, Emperor of India
rows.Notes: Although Edward VIII abdicated, his coins never properly entered circulation but it can be assumed his coins had these words.

rows.Latin text: GEORGIUS VI DEI GRATIA BRITANNIARUM OMNIUM REX FIDEI DEFENSOR INDIÆ IMPERATOR
rows.English text: George VI , by the Grace of God, of all the Britains King, Defender of the Faith, Emperor of India

rows.Latin text: GEORGIUS VI DEI GRATIA BRITANNIARUM OMNIUM REX FIDEI DEFENSOR
rows.English text: George VI , by the Grace of God, of all the Britains King, Defender of the Faith
rows.Notes: The title "Emperor of India" was relinquished in 1948, after the independence of India and Pakistan.

rows.Latin text: ELIZABETH II DEI GRATIA BRITANNIARUM OMNIUM REGINA FIDEI DEFENSOR
rows.English text: Elizabeth II , by the Grace of God, of all the Britains Queen, Defender of the Faith

rows.Latin text: ELIZABETH II DEI GRATIA REGINA FIDEI DEFENSOR
rows.English text: Elizabeth II , by the Grace of God, Queen, Defender of the Faith
rows.Notes: The "of all the Britains" was dropped from the coinage in 1954, and current coins do not name any realm.

rows.Latin text: CHARLES III DEI GRATIA REX FIDEI DEFENSOR
rows.English text: Charles III , by the Grace of God, King, Defender of the Faith

rows.Description: A story arc in Journey into Mystery , "The Fire Next Time", featured Natasha.

rows.Title: Black Widow*
rows.Description: The Marvel Knights limited series, titled "The Itsy Bitsy Spider", has Natasha question her claim to the role of Black Widow when she is challenged by the younger spy Yelena as both track down a biotoxin. Grayson and Jones first introduced Yelena in Inhumans #5 to use her in this series.

rows.Title: Black Widow*
rows.Description: The second volume of Black Widow features Natasha and Yelena.

rows.Title: Black Widow: Pale Little Spider †
rows.Description: Pale Little Spider , published under the adults-only Max imprint, was the first solo series featuring Yelena.

rows.Title: Black Widow
rows.Description: The third volume of Black Widow encompasses the "Homecoming" story arc. Natasha returns to Russia while tracking enemy spies, and she learns that her past is a false memory. Morgan portrays Natasha as more violent and more willing to kill than other writers have.

rows.Title: Black Widow: The Things They Say About Her
rows.Description: The "Homecoming" story was followed by a direct sequel. In this series, Natasha goes into hiding as Nick Fury and Daredevil hunt her on behalf of S.H.I.E.L.D.  Yelena appears as a supporting character in some issues.

rows.Title: Black Widow: Deadly Origin
rows.Description: Deadly Origin tells Natasha's history through flashbacks, using the framing device of revisiting people from her past because she had spread nanites to them.  : 38

rows.Title: Black Widow & the Marvel Girls
rows.Description: This series pairs Natasha with a different female character each issue: Enchantress , the Wasp , Ms. Marvel , and Storm , respectively.

rows.Title: Black Widow
rows.Description: The fourth volume of Black Widow features two story arcs. The first five issues by Liu and Acuña were titled "Name of the Rose". This continued the espionage-focused storytelling following the release of Iron Man 2 .  The latter three issues by Swierczynski and Garcia were titled "Kiss and Kill".

rows.Title: Widowmaker
rows.Description: A continuation of both Black Widow and Hawkeye & Mockingbird , this series follows the three heroes as they search for a spy-killer using Hawkeye's old alias " Ronin ".

rows.Title: Fear Itself: Black Widow
rows.Description: A one-shot was published as part of the Fear Itself event, featuring Natasha as she works with Peregrine on a mission in France. Besides this issue, Natasha does not play a significant role in the event overall.

rows.Title: Captain America and Black Widow
rows.Description: Between Captain America #620 and #640, the series featured various heroes alongside Captain America and the title changed whenever a new character joined him. Captain America and Black Widow featured Captain America and Natasha as they encountered alternate universes.

rows.Title: Black Widow
rows.Description: The fifth volume of Black Widow was published as part of the Marvel Now! branding. This series shifts away from the direct action back toward the character focus developed by Grayson in 1999.

rows.Title: Black Widow
rows.Description: The sixth volume of Black Widow focuses on elements from the character's adaptation in the Marvel Cinematic Universe , placing emphasis on two elements familiar to the movie audience: S.H.I.E.L.D. and the Red Room .

rows.Title: Secret Empire: Uprising
rows.Description: Published as part of the Secret Empire event, this issue features Natasha training the Champions to be spies.

rows.Title: Infinity Countdown: Black Widow
rows.Description: A one-shot featuring Natasha was published as part of the " Infinity Countdown " event. It features Natasha wielding the Space Stone .

rows.Title: Black Widow
rows.Description: The seventh volume of Black Widow features Natasha working with Tyger Tiger to shut down a live streamed torture facility in Madripoor .

rows.Title: Web of Black Widow
rows.Description: A five part limited series featuring Natasha

rows.Title: Black Widow *
rows.Description: The eighth volume of Black Widow consists of three major story arcs. "The Ties That Bind" in issues #1–5 has Natasha brainwashed into thinking she is an architect with a fiancé and son while her allies try to rescue her. "I Am the Black Widow" in issues #7–10 has her working alongside Yelena (as the White Widow), Anya Corazon , and Lucy Nguyen. "Die By the Blade" in #12–15 has the same team work with Hawkeye and the Winter Soldier to fight the Living Blade.

rows.Title: Black Widow: Widow's Sting
rows.Description: The Widow's Sting one-shot features Natasha in a story with more traditional espionage tropes.  It follows her as she fights against Silvermane .

rows.Title: Widowmakers: Red Guardian and Yelena Belova †
rows.Description: A one-shot featuring Yelena and Red Guardian

rows.Title: Black Widow Infinity Comic
rows.Description: A one-shot featuring Natasha and Hawkeye

rows.Title: Wastelanders: Black Widow †
rows.Description: Five one-shot comics were published as an adaptation of the Marvel's Wastelanders podcast set in the post-apocalypse world of Old Man Logan . Wastelanders: Black Widow features an older version of Yelena.

rows.Title: White Widow †
rows.Description: A four part limited series featuring Yelena

rows.Title: Black Widow & Hawkeye
rows.Description: The "Broken Arrow" story arc features Natasha bonded with a symbiote alongside Hawkeye as they fight Damon Dran .

rows.Title: Black Widow: Venomous
rows.Description: A one-shot featuring Natasha bonded with a symbiote as a prologue to the Venom War story arc

rows.Title: Venom War: Venomous
rows.Description: Features Natasha and Anti-Venom ( Flash Thompson )

The game is still available for purchase within Australia via the Online Steam Store , as of May 2022.

rows.Reason: Banned because of a scene of sexual violence.    Devolver Digital reapplied for an International Age Rating Coalition rating ahead of the Nintendo Switch release in August 2019. The game is still banned in Australia, retaining the Refused Classification status.

rows.Name: South Park: The Stick of Truth (2014)
rows.Reason: Banned because of scenes of sexual violence involving minors. Those censored scenes involved the underaged main character getting anally probed by aliens, giving an abortion and receiving one. A version was released replacing those scenes with a card of a koala crying humorously explaining what has been cut.

rows.Name: Saints Row IV (2013)
rows.Reason: Banned because of implied sexual violence and drug use related to incentives and rewards. An appeal was lodged but failed, though the content involving sexual violence was overturned, the drug use was not. An edited version was released lacking a mission involving "Alien Narcotics".

rows.Name: State of Decay (2013)
rows.Reason: Banned because of drug use related to incentives and rewards.  A censored version that changes the drugs to vitamins was later released with an R18+.

rows.Name: Syndicate (2012)
rows.Reason: Banned because of high impact bloody violence.

rows.Name: The Witcher 2: Assassins of Kings (2011)
rows.Reason: Banned because of sexuality and nudity in relation to incentives and rewards. A side quest was given an edit (where a choice to accept sex as a reward is automatically turned down) and the game was subsequently re-rated MA15+.

rows.Name: Risen (2009)
rows.Reason: Banned because of sexual activity and drug use related to incentives and rewards.

rows.Name: Shellshock 2: Blood Trails (2009)
rows.Reason: Banned because of high impact bloody violence.

rows.Name: CrimeCraft (2009)
rows.Reason: The always-on DRM game was banned because of drug use related to incentives and rewards.  The game's servers were shut down in 2017, rendering it unplayable worldwide.

rows.Name: NecroVisioN (2009)
rows.Reason: Banned because of high impact bloody violence.  A censored version was later released with an M rating.

rows.Name: Silent Hill: Homecoming (2008)
rows.Reason: Banned because of a high impact torture scene involving drilling into body parts.  A censored version was later released with an MA15+ rating, changing the angles of said scene.

rows.Name: Dark Sector (2008)
rows.Reason: Banned because of high impact bloody violence.   A censored version was later released with an MA15+ rating.

rows.Name: Manhunt 2 (2007)
rows.Reason: Not officially banned, but the game was never submitted to the ACB over fears that it would be refused classification.

rows.Name: Soldier of Fortune: Payback (2007)
rows.Reason: Banned because of high impact bloody violence.  A censored version was later released with an MA15+ rating, disabling the ability to mutilate enemies.

rows.Name: Marc Eckō's Getting Up: Contents Under Pressure (2006)
rows.Reason: Originally released with an MA15+ rating. Federal Attorney-General Philip Ruddock later appealed the rating, banning it for high impact themes involving the glorification of graffiti.   The game is still available to purchase on Steam  and has not been removed from Steam as of May 2022.

rows.Name: Reservoir Dogs (2006)
rows.Reason: Banned because of high impact violence and torture.

rows.Name: 50 Cent: Bulletproof (2005)
rows.Reason: Banned because of high impact bloody violence.  After an appeal it was Refused Classification once again on 24 November 2005.   A censored version was later released with an MA15+ rating.

rows.Name: Narc (2005)
rows.Reason: Banned because of drug use related to incentives and rewards.

rows.Name: Blitz: The League (2005)
rows.Reason: Banned because of drug use related to incentives and rewards.

rows.Name: Leisure Suit Larry: Magna Cum Laude (2004)
rows.Reason: Banned because of sexuality and nudity in relation to incentives and rewards.  However, it is still available for purchase on Steam as of May 2022  , albeit without a classification.

rows.Name: Manhunt (2003)
rows.Reason: Originally rated MA15+.  Federal Attorney-General Philip Ruddock later appealed the rating in September 2004, banning it because of high impact violence involving torture.

rows.Name: Singles: Flirt Up Your Life (2003)
rows.Reason: Banned because of sexuality and nudity in relation to incentives and rewards.

rows.Name: The Getaway (2002)
rows.Reason: Originally released uncut with a MA15+,  it was later resubmitted and banned due to a scene of detailed torture.  A censored version omitting this scene was later released with a MA15+ rating.

rows.Name: BMX XXX (2002)
rows.Reason: Banned because of high impact sexual references.    A censored version was later released with an MA15+ rating.

rows.Name: Enzai: Falsely Accused (2002)
rows.Reason: Banned by the Australian Communications and Media Authority because of sexual violence involving a person who is, or appears to be, a child under 18 years.

rows.Name: WANDER LUST (1996)
rows.Reason: Likely banned because of sexual activity and/or nudity related to incentives and rewards. The Victorian Police were the applicants for the Refused Classification Rating.

rows.Name: Phantasmagoria (1995)
rows.Reason: Banned because of a scene involving sexual violence. In 2016, the game became available for purchase on Steam without classification and has yet to be taken down as of May 2023  .

rows.Name: DreamWeb (1994)
rows.Reason: Was originally released unrated. Later banned because of a scene of sexual violence. A censored edition was later released with an M rating.   Released as freeware in 2012.

rows.Name: Voyeur (1993)
rows.Reason: Was originally released unrated. Later banned because of high impact sexual themes involving incest.

rows.Name: Porntris (1993)
rows.Reason: Banned because of nudity related to incentives and rewards. The Victorian Police were the applicants for the Refused Classification Rating.

rows.Name: Teresa: House Guest (1993)
rows.Reason: Banned likely because of sexual activity and/or nudity related to incentives and rewards. The Victorian Police were the applicants for the Refused Classification Rating.

rows.Name: Vida X (1993)
rows.Reason: Banned likely because of sexual activity and/or nudity related to incentives and rewards. The Victorian Police were the applicants for the Refused Classification Rating.

rows.Name: Sorority House (1991)
rows.Reason: Banned likely because of sexual activity and/or nudity related to incentives and rewards. The New South Wales Police were the applicants for the Refused Classification Rating.   The game was refused a second time after an appeal by the games developer 3D Realms.

rows.Name: Strip Blackjack (1991)
rows.Reason: Banned because of nudity related to incentives and rewards. The Victorian Police were the applicants for the Refused Classification Rating.

rows.Name: Strip Poker Three (1991)
rows.Reason: Banned because of nudity related to incentives and rewards. The Victorian Police were the applicants for the Refused Classification Rating.

rows.Name: Pocket Gal 2 (1988)
rows.Reason: Banned likely because of sexual activity and/or nudity related to incentives and rewards. Chien Thon Yeun was the applicant.

table_name.header_chain: List of banned video games in Australia > List of video games refused classification > Overturned
table_name.additional_text: The list below includes games where the Australian edition is identical to that of other countries because either: the rating has successfully been appealed, the worldwide edition has later been released in Australia unedited ("uncut"), or the game has received a worldwide edit.

rows.Name: Postal 4: No Regerts (2023)
rows.Reason: Banned by IARC for illicit or proscribed drug use related to incentives or rewards.  Re-rated R18+ on 6 June 2024.

rows.Name: Song of Memories (2018)
rows.Reason: Originally banned because of implied sexual violence.  The game was later rated R18+ through the IARC system in 2023.

rows.Name: Hell Pie (2022)
rows.Reason: Originally refused classification by the IARC for interactive drug use.  Following a review by the Australian Classification Review Board in August 2022, its drug use was found to be justified by context, "the depiction of cannabis within the game, although interactive, is not detailed or realistic.", and was subsequently re-classified R 18+.

rows.Name: Rimworld (2018)
rows.Reason: Originally refused classification because of drug use related to incentives and rewards.  Following a review by the Australian Classification Review Board in April 2022, its drug use was found to be justified by context, as "the game mechanic ultimately provides disincentives related to drug-taking behaviour, to the point where regular drug use leads to negative consequences such as overdose, addiction, and withdrawal", and was subsequently re-classified R 18+.

rows.Name: Disco Elysium: The Final Cut (2021)
rows.Reason: Originally banned because of drug use related to incentives and rewards.     Later given an R18+ rating in May 2021 after the Classification Board agreed that player performance showed negative impacts from depictions of drug use.

rows.Name: The Medium (2020)
rows.Reason: Originally banned due to References to sexual violence through the IARC System.  Rating later appealed and overturned.

rows.Name: Katana Zero (2019)
rows.Reason: Originally banned through the IARC System because of drug use related to incentives and rewards.   Rating later appealed and overturned.

rows.Name: DayZ (2018)
rows.Reason: Originally passed with a MA15+, but was banned upon its PlayStation 4 release because of drug use related to incentives and rewards. Edited worldwide with this edition receiving an MA15+ rating.

rows.Name: We Happy Few (2018)
rows.Reason: Originally banned because of drug use related to incentives and rewards.  The game was re-rated R18+ after a review was conducted with input from Gearbox Software , the game's publisher.

rows.Name: Outlast 2 (2017)
rows.Reason: Originally banned because of implied sexual violence.    The game was resubmitted without the scene and received an R18+ rating. The updated rating reflects the modified version of the game that was later released worldwide. The developer has said that the scene was taken from an 'alpha' version.

rows.Name: Paranautical Activity (2016)
rows.Reason: Banned because of drug use related to incentives and rewards.  It was then re-classified as M for Mature Themes on January 16, 2016.  On 25 April 2018, the game was re-classified as MA 15+ for Strong Themes, this classification has remained since.

rows.Name: Hotline Miami (2012)
rows.Reason: Originally rated MA15+ on 7 May 2013 by the classification board.  It was later re-rated R18+ on 28 May 2015 through the IARC System.   On 13 June 2019 it was refused classification through the IARC System after Devolver Digital attempted to get the game reclassified for the release of the Hotline Miami Collection .  On 14 May 2022, Hotline Miami received a MA15+ rating.

rows.Name: The House of the Dead: Overkill Extended Cut (2011)
rows.Reason: Originally banned due to high impact bloody violence.  Sega successfully appealed the rating on the basis that the over the top violence mitigated the impact.

rows.Name: Mortal Kombat (2011)
rows.Reason: Originally banned because of high impact bloody violence.   The Komplete Edition was later rated R18+ in 2013 after the said rating was introduced.

rows.Name: Aliens vs. Predator (2010)
rows.Reason: Originally banned because of high impact bloody violence. Rating later appealed and overturned.

rows.Name: Left 4 Dead 2 (2009)
rows.Reason: Originally banned due to high impact bloody violence. A version has been released using the same censoring as Germany.   On October 7, 2009, the uncensored version was passed with an MA15+ Rating.  On 29 August 2014, the rating was raised to R18+.

rows.Name: Sexy Poker (2009)
rows.Reason: Originally banned because of nudity in relation to incentives and rewards.   Edited worldwide with this edition receiving an M rating.

rows.Name: F.E.A.R. 2: Project Origin (2009)
rows.Reason: Originally banned because of high impact bloody violence. The decision was later appealed on the basis that the violence was unrealistic.

rows.Name: Fallout 3 (2008)
rows.Reason: Originally banned due to drug use related to incentives and rewards.  Edited worldwide due to the small change needed (the name of morphine was changed to Med-X).

rows.Name: The Punisher (2004)
rows.Reason: Originally banned because of high impact violence involving torture.  Edited worldwide due to international trouble (threats of receiving an AO rating in America and being deemed as "objectionable material" in the UK). This edition was passed, receiving an MA15+.

rows.Name: Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas (2004)
rows.Reason: Had its classification revoked on August 16, 2005, following the Hot Coffee controversy .  Edited worldwide with this version of the game also achieving an MA15+.

rows.Name: Shellshock: Nam '67 (2004)
rows.Reason: Originally banned because of sexual violence and drug use related to incentives and rewards.  Edited worldwide with this version receiving an MA15+ rating for Medium level animated violence, Adult themes, Sexual references and Drug references.

rows.Name: Silverball: Product Version 8 (2003)
rows.Reason: Originally banned because of sexuality and nudity in relation to incentives and rewards.  Rating was later appealed and re-rated to an unrestricted M on the basis that the nude static images were incidental to gameplay rather than as a reward.

rows.Name: Postal 2 (2003)
rows.Reason: Originally banned due to "high impact" violence.  In October 2013, the game was given a R18+ rating after a request from the Australian Communications and Media Authority (ACMA), and listed for sale on digital storefronts.    However, since Postal 2 was never submitted for re-classification by the game's publisher, it technically remained banned and was removed from digital storefronts in April 2024.  In July 2024, the game was submitted again, and was re-rated with an MA15+ classification, officially lifting the ban after nineteen years. The game has been available for purchase on Steam as of June 2025.

rows.Name: Grand Theft Auto III (2001)
rows.Reason: Originally released uncut with an MA15+, it was later banned due to sexual violence involving prostitutes.   A censored version lacking the ability to pick up prostitutes was later released with an MA15+.  On 26 September 2019, a version restoring the use of prostitutes was rated R18+.

rows.Name: Tender Loving Care (1998)
rows.Reason: Originally banned because of high-impact sexual references and nudity.  Later submitted as a DVD due to being more of an interactive live-action movie than a videogame. Due to being under different guidelines it was re-rated MA15+.

rows.Name: Postal (1997)
rows.Reason: Originally banned because of high impact themes involving depictions of revolting and abhorrent content.  In December 2019, game was released as freeware and is available on the Australian versions of Steam and GOG.com  On 5 April 2020, the remastered version, Postal Redux , was passed through the IARC System with an MA15+.

rows.Name: Duke Nukem 3D (1996)
rows.Reason: Originally banned because of sexual violence.  Later released uncensored with an MA15+ rating.

rows.Name: Wijaya Dahanayake
rows.Notes: Deputy Minister of Public Administration and Home Affairs and Member of Parliament for Matara

rows.Name: Lionel Premasiri
rows.Notes: Member for Galle District (2004–10) and deputy minister of Social Services and Social Welfare

rows.Name: Weeranarayana Kelum Seneviratne
rows.Notes: At the local government elections in 2006 Seneviratne and de Silva both received an equal number (5,998) preferences each and subsequently agreed to share the office of Mayor, with Seneviratne becoming mayor for the first two years.

rows.Name: Alexendar Methsiri de Silva
rows.Notes: At the 2011 local government elections de Silva was formally elected as mayor. In January 2013 the Chief Minister of Southern Province , Shan Wijayalal De Silva formally removed de Silva from the office of mayor.

rows.Name: Weeranarayana Kelum Seneviratne
rows.Notes: Following the removal of de Silva the deputy mayor, Seneviratne, was appointed as mayor.

rows.Name: Alexandar Methsiri de Silva
rows.Notes: In June 2014 the Galle High Court revoked the Chief Minister's decision to remove de Silva as mayor and he was re-instated.

rows.Name: Weeranarayana Kelum Seneviratne
rows.Notes: In May 2015 the Court of Appeal annulled the Galle High Court's decision and Seneviratne was appointed as mayor.

rows.Name: Priyantha Godagama Sahabandu
rows.Notes: Subsequent to the 2018 Sri Lankan local elections , in a secret ballot held on 23 March 2018, Sahabandu was elected to the position of mayor obtaining 20 votes to 11 over his rival candidate.

rows.Name: Halvitigala Ihala Gamage Sunil
rows.Notes: Following the 2025 Sri Lankan local elections , Galle MC voted 19–17 for a secret ballot. NPP 's Halvitigala Ihala Gamage Sunil was elected Mayor with 19 votes.
